title.zh: 卷一百〇六 列傳第五十六: 李林甫 楊國忠 張暐 王琚 王毛仲 陳玄禮
title.en: Volume 106 Biographies 56: Li Linfu, Yang Guozhong, Zhang Wei, Wang Ju, Wang Maozhong, Chen Xuanli
title.raw: 卷一百〇六 列傳第五十六: 李林甫 楊國忠 張暐 王琚 王毛仲 陳玄禮 Volume 106 Biographies 56: Li Linfu, Yang Guozhong, Zhang Wei, Wang Ju, Wang Maozhong, Chen Xuanli

sentences.zh: 李林甫楊國忠張暐王琚王毛仲陳玄禮附

translations.literal: Li Linfu, Yang Guozhong, Zhang Wei, Wang Ju, Wang Maozhong, Chen Xuanli — appended biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Li Linfu, Yang Guozhong, Zhang Wei, Wang Ju, Wang Maozhong, and Chen Xuanli (with appended notices).

sentences.zh: 李林甫，高祖從父弟長平王叔良之曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Linfu was the great-grandson of Prince Changping, Shuliang, a younger cousin of Emperor Gaozu on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was a great-grandson of Prince Changping, Shuliang, who was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 叔良生孝斌，官至原州長史。

translations.literal: Shuliang begot Xiaobin, who reached the office of Administrator of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang's son was Xiaobin, who rose to be administrator of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝斌生思誨，官至揚府參軍，思誨即林甫之父也。

translations.literal: Xiaobin begot Sihui, who reached the office of Staff Officer in Yang Prefecture; Sihui was Linfu's father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobin had a son, Sihui, who served as a staff officer in Yang Prefecture; Sihui was Li Linfu's father.

sentences.zh: 林甫善音律，初為千牛直長，其舅楚國公姜皎深愛之。

translations.literal: Linfu was skilled in music; he first served as Chief of the Thousand-Ox Guard, and his maternal uncle, Duke of Chu, Jiang Jiao, loved him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was accomplished in music. He began his career as chief of the Thousand-Ox Guard, and his uncle, the Duke of Chu, Jiang Jiao, was deeply fond of him.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷太子中允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, he was transferred to be a Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign, he was appointed a companion in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 時源乾曜為侍中，乾曜侄孫光乘，姜皎妹婿，乾曜與之親。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Qianyao was Vice Director of the Secretariat; Qianyao's grandnephew Guangcheng was Jiang Jiao's son-in-law by marriage to his sister, and Qianyao was close to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Qianyao served as vice director of the Secretariat. His grandnephew Guangcheng had married a sister of Jiang Jiao, and Qianyao was on close terms with the family.

sentences.zh: 乾曜之男潔白其父曰：「李林甫求為司門郎中。」

translations.literal: Qianyao's son Jie told his father: "Li Linfu seeks appointment as Director of the Gate Office."
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao's son Jie told his father, "Li Linfu is asking to be made director of the Gate Office."

sentences.zh: 乾曜曰：「郎官須有素行才望高者，哥奴豈是郎官耶？」

translations.literal: Qianyao said: "Directors must have longstanding conduct and high reputation and talent — how could Genu be a director?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao replied, "A director's post requires a man of established conduct and real standing. How could Genu ever qualify as a director?"

sentences.zh: 數日，除諭德。

translations.literal: Within several days, [Linfu] was appointed Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, Li Linfu was named preceptor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 哥奴，林甫小字。

translations.literal: Genu was Linfu's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Genu was Li Linfu's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子司業。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to become vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十四年，宇文融為御史中丞，引之同列，因拜御史中丞，歷刑、吏二侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Yuwen Rong was Censor-in-Chief and brought him into the same rank; he was then appointed Censor-in-Chief and served successively as Vice Minister of Justice and of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen of Kaiyuan, when Yuwen Rong was censor-in-chief, he brought Li Linfu onto the same level of office. Linfu was then made censor-in-chief himself and later served as vice minister of justice and of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時武惠妃愛傾後宮，二子壽王、盛王以母愛特見寵異，太子瑛益疏薄。

translations.literal: At that time Consort Wu Hui's favor dominated the inner palace; her two sons, the Prince of Shou and the Prince of Sheng, because of their mother's love received exceptional favor, while the Heir Apparent Ying grew ever more estranged.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort Wu Hui's favor held sway over the inner palace. Her sons, the Princes of Shou and Sheng, were singled out for special affection on their mother's account, while Crown Prince Ying grew increasingly distant from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 林甫多與中貴人善，乃因中官白惠妃云：「願保護壽王。」

translations.literal: Linfu was on good terms with many of the inner eunuchs; he therefore had a eunuch tell Consort Wu Hui: "I wish to protect the Prince of Shou."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu cultivated ties with many senior eunuchs and had one of them tell Consort Wu Hui, "I wish to safeguard the Prince of Shou."

sentences.zh: 惠妃德之。

translations.literal: The consort was grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was deeply obliged to him.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中裴光庭妻武三思女，詭譎有材略，與林甫私。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director Pei Guangting's wife was a daughter of Wu Sansi; she was crafty and had talent and stratagem, and was intimate with Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the wife of Vice Director Pei Guangting had been a daughter of Wu Sansi. She was cunning and capable, and carried on a secret affair with Li Linfu.

sentences.zh: 中官高力士本出三思家，及光庭卒，武氏銜哀祈於力士，請林甫代其夫位，力士未敢言，玄宗使中書令蕭嵩擇相，嵩久之以右丞韓休對，玄宗然之，乃令草詔。

translations.literal: The eunuch Gao Lishi had originally come from Sansi's household; when Guangting died, the Wu woman, bearing grief, pleaded with Lishi to ask that Linfu replace her husband's position. Lishi did not dare speak. Xuanzong had Chief Minister Xiao Song select a chancellor; after a long while Song answered with Right Vice Director Han Xiu. The emperor approved and ordered the edict drafted.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Gao Lishi had originally been attached to Wu Sansi's household. When Guangting died, the Wu woman, in mourning, begged Lishi to have Li Linfu take her husband's place. Lishi did not dare raise it. The emperor ordered Chief Minister Xiao Song to choose a new chancellor. Song hesitated a long while, then named Han Xiu, the right vice director. Xuanzong agreed and had the appointment edict drafted.

sentences.zh: 力士遽漏於武氏，乃令林甫白休。

translations.literal: Lishi hastily leaked it to the Wu woman, who then had Linfu inform Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi quickly let the secret slip to the Wu woman, and she had Li Linfu warn Han Xiu.

sentences.zh: 休既入相，甚德林甫，與嵩不和，乃薦林甫堪為宰相，惠妃陰助之，因拜黃門侍郎，玄宗眷遇益深。

translations.literal: Once Xiu had entered the chancellorship, he was deeply grateful to Linfu; he was at odds with Song and therefore recommended Linfu as fit to be chancellor. Consort Hui secretly assisted, and [Linfu] was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; the emperor's favor toward him grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Once Han Xiu became chancellor, he felt greatly indebted to Li Linfu. At odds with Xiao Song, he recommended Linfu as chancellor material, while Consort Hui worked for him behind the scenes. Li Linfu was made vice director of the Palace Secretariat, and the emperor's regard for him deepened further.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以黃門侍郎平章事裴耀卿為侍中，中書侍郎平章事張九齡為中書令，林甫為禮部尚書、同中書門下三品，並加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Palace Secretariat Vice Director and Associate Director Pei Yaoqing was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Secretariat Vice Director and Associate Director Zhang Jiuling was made Chief of the Secretariat; Linfu was made Minister of Rites and Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank, all receiving the title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, Pei Yaoqing, who had served as vice director of the Palace Secretariat with associate director status, was made vice director of the Secretariat; Zhang Jiuling, a Secretariat vice director with the same rank, was made chief of the Secretariat; and Li Linfu was made minister of rites and associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the third rank, with the title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness conferred on all three.

sentences.zh: 林甫面柔而有狡計，能伺侯人主意，故驟歷清列，為時委任。

translations.literal: Linfu's face was gentle but he had crafty schemes; he could observe and await others' intentions, and therefore swiftly passed through pure offices and was entrusted by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had a mild manner but a devious mind. He was adept at reading others' intentions, rose rapidly through the highest offices, and won the trust of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 而中官妃家，皆厚結托，伺上動靜，皆預知之，故出言進奏，動必稱旨。

translations.literal: Moreover, with inner eunuchs and the consort's kin he formed thick bonds of patronage; observing the emperor's movements, he knew them all in advance, so that when he spoke in memorials, his words always matched the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He also cultivated close ties with senior eunuchs and the consort's family, learning the emperor's moods in advance. Whatever he submitted in memorials invariably struck the right note.

sentences.zh: 而猜忌陰中人，不見於詞色，朝廷受主恩顧，不由其門，則構成其罪；

translations.literal: Yet he was suspicious and secretly struck at people without showing it in word or countenance; if anyone at court who received the ruler's grace and favor did not pass through his gate, he would fabricate crimes against them;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was suspicious and struck at people from the shadows, never betraying it in speech or expression. Anyone at court who enjoyed the emperor's favor but did not come through his door would find crimes fabricated against them;

sentences.zh: 與之善者，雖廝養下士，盡至榮寵。

translations.literal: those on good terms with him, even grooms and menial servants, all reached glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: while those he favored, even stable boys and men of the lowest rank, could rise to the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 尋歷戶、兵二尚書，知政事如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he served successively as Minister of Revenue and of War, handling state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: He soon held the ministries of revenue and of war in succession, while continuing to direct state affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 尋又以太子瑛、鄂王瑤、光王琚皆以母失愛而有怨言，駙馬都尉楊洄白惠妃。

translations.literal: Soon again, because the Heir Apparent Ying, the Prince of E, Yao, and the Prince of Guang, Ju, all had lost their mothers' favor and bore resentful words, the Commandant-escort Yang Hui informed Consort Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because Crown Prince Ying and the Princes of E and Guang had all lost their mothers' favor and were heard to complain, Commandant-escort Yang Hui reported this to Consort Hui.

sentences.zh: 玄宗怒，謀於宰臣，將罪之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was angry and consulted the chief ministers, intending to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was furious and took counsel with his chief ministers, intending to punish the princes.

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「陛下三個成人兒不可得。

translations.literal: Jiuling said: "Your Majesty cannot do without these three grown sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling said, "Your Majesty, you cannot afford to lose these three grown sons.

sentences.zh: 太子國本，長在宮中，受陛下義方，人未見過，陛下奈何以喜怒間忍欲廢之？

translations.literal: The heir is the state's foundation; he has long dwelt in the palace and received Your Majesty's moral instruction; no fault of his has been seen — how can Your Majesty, between anger and joy, bear in your heart the wish to depose him?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the foundation of the state. He has long lived in the palace under Your Majesty's instruction, and no fault has been seen in him. How can Your Majesty, in a moment of anger, contemplate deposing him?

sentences.zh: 臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Your servant dares not accept the decree."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not obey such an order.

sentences.zh: 玄宗不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 林甫惘然而退，初無言，既而謂中貴人曰：「家事何須謀及於人。」

translations.literal: Linfu withdrew in a daze; at first he said nothing, then afterward told a senior eunuch: "Household affairs — why must they be deliberated with others?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu withdrew looking blank. At first he said nothing; then he told a senior eunuch, "Family matters — why consult outsiders about them?

sentences.zh: 時朔方節度使牛仙客在鎮，有政能，玄宗加實封，九齡又奏曰：「邊將馴兵秣馬，儲蓄軍實，常務耳，陛下賞之可也；

translations.literal: At that time the Military Commissioner of Shuofang, Niu Xianke, was at his post and had administrative ability; Xuanzong added to his substantive fief. Jiuling again memorialized: "Border generals training troops and feeding horses and storing military stores are routine duties — Your Majesty may reward that;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Niu Xianke, military commissioner of Shuofang, was at his post and had proved capable. The emperor wished to add to his substantive fief. Zhang Jiuling memorialized again: "For a frontier commander to drill troops, provision horses, and stockpile supplies is routine duty — Your Majesty may reward that;

sentences.zh: 欲賜實賦，恐未得宜。

translations.literal: to wish to grant a substantive fief revenue may perhaps not be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: but to grant him revenue from a substantive fief may not be appropriate.

sentences.zh: 惟聖慮思之。」

translations.literal: May Your Sagely consideration reflect on it."
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 林甫以其言告仙客，仙客翌日見上，泣讓官爵。

translations.literal: Linfu told Xianke his words; the next day Xianke saw the emperor and, weeping, declined rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu relayed Zhang's words to Niu Xianke, who the next day appeared before the emperor in tears and declined further honors.

sentences.zh: 玄宗欲行實封之命，兼為尚書，九齡執奏如初。

translations.literal: Xuanzong wished to carry out the order for the substantive fief and also make him Minister; Jiuling persisted in memorializing as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still meant to grant the substantive fief and appoint Xianke minister. Zhang Jiuling argued as before.

sentences.zh: 帝變色曰：「事總由卿？」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: "Are affairs entirely up to you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression darkened. "Must everything be decided by you?" he said.

sentences.zh: 九齡頓首曰：「陛下使臣待罪宰相，事有未允，臣合盡言。

translations.literal: Jiuling knocked his head and said: "Your Majesty made your servant hold the chancellorship while awaiting punishment; when affairs are not acceptable, your servant ought to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty appointed me chancellor on sufferance. When something is not right, it is my duty to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 違忤聖情，合當萬死。」

translations.literal: To go against the sagely feeling merits ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: If I have offended Your Majesty, I deserve death ten thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「卿以仙客無門籍耶？

translations.literal: Xuanzong said: "Do you think Xianke has no pedigree in the gates of office?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said, "Do you think Xianke lacks a distinguished lineage?

sentences.zh: 卿有何門閥？」

translations.literal: What gate and clan do you have?"
translations.idiomatic: What lineage do you claim?"

sentences.zh: 九齡對曰：「臣荒僥微賤，仙客中華之士。

translations.literal: Jiuling replied: "Your servant is crude, fortunate, and meanly born; Xianke is a man of the central domains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling answered, "I am a man of humble and obscure birth. Xianke is a subject of the central heartland.

sentences.zh: 然陛下擢臣踐臺閣，掌綸誥；

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty raised your servant to tread the terrace and pavilion and handle imperial rescripts;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty raised me to the highest offices and entrusted me with imperial edicts;

sentences.zh: 仙客本河湟一使典，目不識文字，若大任之，臣恐非宜。」

translations.literal: Xianke was originally a petty clerk from the Hehuang region and does not recognize written characters — if he were given a great appointment, your servant fears it would not be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Xianke was once a minor clerk from the Hehuang frontier and cannot even read. To give him a weighty post, I fear, would not be wise."

sentences.zh: 林甫退而言曰：「但有材識，何必辭學；

translations.literal: Linfu withdrew and then said: "So long as there is talent and insight, why must there be literary learning;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Li Linfu remarked, "If a man has talent and judgment, why demand literary learning?

sentences.zh: 天子用人，何有不可？」

translations.literal: when the Son of Heaven employs men, what cannot be done?
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven chooses his servants, what is impossible?

sentences.zh: 玄宗滋不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 九齡與中書侍郎嚴挺之善。

translations.literal: Jiuling was on good terms with Secretariat Vice Director Yan Tingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling was close to Yan Tingzhi, vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 挺之初娶妻出之，妻乃嫁蔚州刺史王元琰。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had first taken a wife and divorced her; the wife then married Wang Yuanyan, Prefect of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had once married a woman and then divorced her; she afterward married Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時元琰坐贓，詔三司使推之，挺之救免其罪。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanyan was charged with embezzlement; an edict ordered the Three Offices commissioners to investigate; Tingzhi rescued and exempted him from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyan was accused of corruption, the Three Offices were ordered to investigate. Yan Tingzhi intervened and secured his acquittal.

sentences.zh: 玄宗察之，謂九齡曰：「王元琰不無贓罪，嚴挺之囑托所由輩有顏面。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong investigated and said to Jiuling: "Wang Yuanyan was not without guilt in embezzlement; Yan Tingzhi's entreaties — those through whom he acted still have face."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked into the matter and told Zhang Jiuling, "Wang Yuanyan was not innocent of corruption. Yan Tingzhi's intervention shows that certain officials still had favors to repay.

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「此挺之前妻，今已婚崔氏，不合有情。」

translations.literal: Jiuling said: "This is Tingzhi's former wife; she is now married to the Cui clan — there should be no personal attachment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling replied, "She is Yan's former wife and is now married into the Cui family. There should be no lingering attachment."

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「卿不知，雖離之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong said: "You do not understand — even though divorced,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You do not understand. Even after divorce,

sentences.zh: 亦卻有私。」

translations.literal: there is still private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: private feelings may remain.

sentences.zh: 玄宗籍前事，以九齡有黨，與裴耀卿俱罷知政事，拜左、右丞相，出挺之為洺州刺史，元琰流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, citing earlier affairs, regarded Jiuling as having a faction; together with Pei Yaoqing he removed them from handling state affairs, appointing them Left and Right Chancellors; Tingzhi was sent out as Prefect of Ming Prefecture, and Yuanyan was exiled beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on these earlier matters, the emperor judged that Zhang Jiuling had formed a faction. He and Pei Yaoqing were both removed from directing state affairs and given the nominal posts of left and right chancellor. Yan Tingzhi was sent out as prefect of Ming Prefecture, and Wang Yuanyan was exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 即日林甫代九齡為中書、集賢殿大學士、修國史；

translations.literal: That same day Linfu replaced Jiuling as Chief of the Secretariat, Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and Compiler of the National History;
translations.idiomatic: That same day Li Linfu replaced Zhang as chief of the Secretariat, grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and compiler of the national history;

sentences.zh: 拜牛仙客工部尚書、同中書門下平章事，知門下省事。

translations.literal: Niu Xianke was appointed Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery with the Second Rank, and directed Chancellery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke was made minister of works, associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the second rank, and put in charge of Chancellery business.

sentences.zh: 監察御史周子諒言仙客非宰相器，玄宗怒而殺之。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Zhou Ziliang said Xianke was not material for chancellor; Xuanzong in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Zhou Ziliang declared that Niu Xianke was unfit to be chancellor. The emperor, enraged, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 林甫言子諒本九齡引用，乃貶九齡為荊州長史。

translations.literal: Linfu said Ziliang had originally been introduced by Jiuling, and therefore demoted Jiuling to Administrator of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu argued that Zhou had been Zhang Jiuling's protégé and had Jiuling demoted to administrator of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 林甫既秉樞衡，兼領隴右、河西節度，又加吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Once Linfu held the pivot and balance, he also concurrently headed the Longyou and Hexi military commissions, and was further made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Linfu held the reins of government, he also took charge of the Longyou and Hexi frontier commands and was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 天寶改易官名，為右相，停知節度事，加光祿大夫，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era the official names were changed; he became Right Chancellor, ceased handling military commission affairs, was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianbao reign revised official titles, he became right chancellor, relinquished his frontier commands, received the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六載，加開府儀同三司，賜實封三百戶，而恩渥彌深。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given Palace Equipage of the Third Rank and granted three hundred households of substantive fief, while favor and kindness grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made palace equipage of the third rank and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households, while imperial favor toward him deepened still further.

sentences.zh: 凡禦府膳羞，遠方珍味，中人宣賜，道路相望。

translations.literal: Whenever imperial pantry delicacies and rare flavors from distant regions were announced and bestowed by inner attendants, they filled the roads one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial delicacies and rare foods from distant regions were sent to him by palace attendants in an unbroken stream along the roads.

sentences.zh: 與宰相李適之雖同宗屬，而適之輕率，嘗與林甫同論時政，多失大體，由是主恩益疏，以至罷免。

translations.literal: With Chancellor Li Shizhi, though of the same clan branch, Shizhi was light and rash; he had once discussed current policy with Linfu and often missed the larger pattern, and thereby the ruler's favor grew ever thinner, until he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He and Chancellor Li Shizhi were related, but Shizhi was rash. When they discussed policy together, Shizhi often missed the larger point, and the emperor's favor toward him waned until he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎陳希烈性便佞，嘗曲事林甫，適之既罷，乃引希烈同知政事。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Vice Director Chen Xilie was by nature facile and fawning; he had bent to serve Linfu; once Shizhi was dismissed, [Linfu] brought Xilie in to share handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie, vice director of the Palace Secretariat, was pliant and obsequious by nature and had long curried favor with Li Linfu. After Shizhi's dismissal, Linfu brought Chen in to share direction of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 林甫久典樞衡，天下威權，並歸於己，臺司機務，希烈不敢參議，但唯諾而已。

translations.literal: Linfu had long presided over the pivot and balance; the world's authority and power all returned to himself; in terrace and office business Xilie dared not join in deliberation but only assented.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had long controlled the government, and all real authority in the realm rested with him. In the routine business of the central offices Chen Xilie dared not offer opinions and merely assented.

sentences.zh: 每有奏請，必先賂遺左右，伺察上旨，以固恩寵。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a memorial request, he would first bribe and gift those at the emperor's side, observe the supreme intent, and thereby secure favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Before every memorial he bribed the emperor's attendants to learn the ruler's mood and thus secure his position.

sentences.zh: 上在位多載，倦於萬機，恆以大臣接對拘檢，難徇私欲，自得林甫，一以委成。

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the throne many years and was weary of the myriad affairs; he had always found great ministers' reception and response restrictive and hard to follow private desires — since gaining Linfu, he entrusted everything to completion through him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had reigned many years and wearied of the myriad affairs of state. He had always found audiences with senior ministers constraining and difficult for indulging private wishes. Once he had Li Linfu, he entrusted everything to him.

sentences.zh: 故杜絕逆耳之言，恣行宴樂，衤任席無別，不以為恥，由林甫之贊成也。

translations.literal: Therefore he cut off words that offended the ear, gave free rein to feasts and music, made no distinction in pillow companions, and did not regard it as shame — all through Linfu's support and completion.
translations.idiomatic: He shut out unwelcome counsel, gave himself over to feasting and pleasure, made no distinction among his bed companions, and felt no shame in it — all with Li Linfu's encouragement.

sentences.zh: 林甫京城邸第，田園水硙，利盡上腴。

translations.literal: Linfu's mansions and lodges in the capital, fields, gardens, and water mills — the profit exhausted the finest fertile lands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu's town houses, estates, and water-powered mills in the capital consumed the richest lands in the region.

sentences.zh: 城東有薛王別墅，林亭幽邃，甲於都邑，特以賜之，及女樂二部，天下珍玩，前後賜與，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: East of the city was the Prince of Xue's villa; its wooded pavilions were secluded and deep, foremost in the capital — it was specially bestowed on him, along with two companies of female musicians; rare treasures of the realm, bestowed before and after, could not be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city stood a villa of the Prince of Xue, whose wooded pavilions were the finest in the capital; the emperor gave it to him specially, along with two troupes of female musicians. Rare treasures from across the empire were bestowed on him in such number that they could not all be recorded.

sentences.zh: 宰相用事之盛，開元已來，未有其比。

translations.literal: The fullness of a chancellor's exercise of power since the Kaiyuan era had no parallel.
translations.idiomatic: No chancellor since the Kaiyuan era had wielded power on such a scale.

sentences.zh: 然每事過慎，條理眾務，增修綱紀，中外遷除，皆有恆度。

translations.literal: Yet in every matter he was excessively cautious; he ordered the multitude of affairs, increased and repaired statutes and regulations, and promotions and removals within and without all had fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was meticulous in every matter, set the administration in order, strengthened regulations, and kept promotions and dismissals at court and in the provinces to fixed standards.

sentences.zh: 而耽寵固權，己自封植，朝望稍著，必陰計中傷之。

translations.literal: Yet he clung to favor and secured power, planting and fencing himself in; if court reputation grew slightly prominent, he would surely secretly scheme to strike at and harm them.
translations.idiomatic: He clung to favor and entrenched his power. Anyone at court whose reputation began to rise would inevitably be struck down by his secret machinations.

sentences.zh: 初，韋堅登朝，以堅皇太子妃兄，引居要職，示結恩信，實圖傾之，乃潛令御史中丞楊慎矜陰伺堅隙。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei Jian entered court, because Jian was the elder brother of the crown prince's consort, [Linfu] drew him into a key post, showing bonds of grace and trust while in fact plotting to overturn him; he secretly ordered Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin to watch Jian's gaps in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Jian first came to court, Li Linfu, knowing that Jian was the elder brother of the crown prince's consort, gave him an important post and feigned friendship while plotting his ruin. He secretly ordered Censor-in-Chief Yang Shenjin to watch for a chance to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 會正月望夜，皇太子出遊，與堅相見，慎矜知之，奏上。

translations.literal: It happened on the fifteenth night of the first month that the crown prince went out touring and met with Jian; Shenjin learned of it and memorialized upward.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the Lantern Festival the crown prince went abroad and met Wei Jian. Shenjin learned of it and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，以為不軌，黜堅，免太子妃韋氏。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, regarding it as irregular conduct; Jian was dismissed and the crown prince's consort of the Wei clan was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and judged the conduct treasonous. Wei Jian was dismissed, and the crown prince's Wei consort was deposed.

sentences.zh: 林甫因是奏李適之與堅昵狎，及裴寬、韓朝宗並曲附適之，上以為然，賜堅自盡，裴、韓皆坐之斥逐。

translations.literal: Linfu thereupon memorialized that Li Shizhi was intimate and familiar with Jian, and that Pei Kuan and Han Chaozong all bent to attach themselves to Shizhi; the emperor regarded it as so, granted Jian suicide, and Pei and Han all sat in the matter and were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu then reported that Li Shizhi had been on intimate terms with Wei Jian and that Pei Kuan and Han Chaozong had curried favor with Shizhi. The emperor believed him, ordered Wei Jian to take his own life, and had Pei and Han driven from office.

sentences.zh: 後楊慎矜權位漸盛，林甫又忌之，乃引王鉷為御史中丞，托以心腹。

translations.literal: Later Yang Shenjin's power and position gradually flourished; Linfu again resented him and therefore brought in Wang Hong as Censor-in-Chief, entrusting him as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Yang Shenjin's power grew, Li Linfu grew jealous again and installed Wang Hong as censor-in-chief, treating him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 鉷希林甫意，遂誣罔密奏慎矜左道不法，遂族其家。

translations.literal: Hong hoped to please Linfu's intent and therefore falsely accused him in a secret memorial that Shenjin practiced the left Way and was unlawful; his clan was then exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, eager to please Li Linfu, secretly memorialized that Shenjin practiced heterodox rites and broke the law. The entire Yang clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠以椒房之親，出入中禁，奏請多允，乃擢在臺省，令按刑獄。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong, by kinship of the pepper chambers, went in and out of the inner forbidden precinct; his memorial requests were mostly approved; he was therefore promoted within the terrace offices and ordered to investigate criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, a relative of the imperial consort clan, moved freely within the inner palace, and most of his requests were granted. He was promoted within the censorial and secretariat offices and put in charge of criminal investigations.

sentences.zh: 會皇太子良娣杜氏父有鄰與子婿柳勣不葉，勣飛書告有鄰不法，引李邕為證，詔王鉷與國忠按問。

translations.literal: It happened that the crown prince's secondary consort of the Du clan's father Youlin was at odds with his son-in-law Liu Ji; Ji sent a flying letter reporting Youlin's unlawful conduct, citing Li Yong as witness; an edict ordered Wang Hong and Guozhong to investigate and question.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Youlin, father of the crown prince's Du consort, was estranged from his son-in-law Liu Ji. Ji sent a secret letter accusing Youlin of wrongdoing and named Li Yong as a witness. The emperor ordered Wang Hong and Yang Guozhong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 鉷與國忠附會林甫奏之，於是賜有鄰自盡，出良娣為庶人，李邕、裴敦復枝黨數人並坐極法。

translations.literal: Hong and Guozhong joined Linfu's memorial in agreement; thereupon Youlin was granted suicide, the secondary consort was sent out as a commoner, and Li Yong, Pei Dunfu, and several of their branch factions all sat in the matter and received the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and Yang Guozhong shaped their report to suit Li Linfu. Youlin was ordered to kill himself, the consort was reduced to commoner status, and Li Yong, Pei Dunfu, and several of their associates were executed.

sentences.zh: 林甫之苞藏安忍，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Linfu's harboring and calm endurance of cruelty were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu's secret malice and ruthless patience were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 林甫自以始謀不佐皇太子，慮為後患，故屢起大獄以危之，賴太子重慎無過，流言不入。

translations.literal: Linfu himself thought that from the first his schemes had not aided the crown prince and feared being a later trouble; he therefore repeatedly raised great prosecutions to endanger him, relying on the prince's grave caution and lack of fault so that slander did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu knew that he had never supported the crown prince from the outset and feared future retribution. He repeatedly launched major prosecutions to threaten the heir, but the prince's own caution and innocence kept slander from taking hold.

sentences.zh: 林甫嘗令濟陽別駕魏林告隴右、河西節度使王忠嗣，林往任朔州刺史，忠嗣時為山東節度，自雲與忠王同養宮中，情意相得，欲擁兵以佐太子。

translations.literal: Linfu once had Jiyang Vice Prefect Wei Lin accuse Wang Zhongsi, Military Commissioner of Longyou and Hexi; Lin had formerly served as Prefect of Shuo Prefecture when Zhongsi was then military commissioner of Shandong; he claimed that he and the Prince of Zhong had been raised together in the palace, their feelings in accord, and wished to gather troops to aid the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu once had Wei Lin, vice prefect of Jiyang, accuse Wang Zhongsi, military commissioner of Longyou and Hexi. Lin had once served as prefect of Shuo when Zhongsi held the Shandong command. He claimed that he and Zhongsi had been raised together in the palace, were close in affection, and that Zhongsi meant to gather troops to support the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞之曰：「我兒在內，何路與外人交通？

translations.literal: When Xuanzong heard it he said: "My son is within — what path could there be for communicating with outsiders?
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong heard this he said, "My son is inside the palace. How could he be in contact with outsiders?

sentences.zh: 此妄也。」

translations.literal: This is delusion.
translations.idiomatic: This is nonsense.

sentences.zh: 然忠嗣亦左授漢陽太守。

translations.literal: Yet Zhongsi was also transferred left to be Prefect of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless Wang Zhongsi was demoted to prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 八載，咸寧太府趙奉章告林甫罪狀二十餘條。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Xianning Grand Storehouse Keeper Zhao Fengzhang reported more than twenty articles of Linfu's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao, Zhao Fengzhang of the Xianning Grand Storehouse accused Li Linfu of more than twenty crimes.

sentences.zh: 告未上，林甫知之，諷御史臺逮捕，以為妖言，重杖決殺。

translations.literal: Before the report went up, Linfu learned of it and hinted to the Censorate to arrest him, treating it as demonic speech; he was heavily clubbed and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the accusation reached the throne, Li Linfu learned of it and had the Censorate arrest Zhao on charges of sorcery. He was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 十載，林甫兼領安西大都護、朔方節度，俄兼單於副大都護。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Linfu concurrently headed the Protectorate-General of the Pacified West and the Shuofang military commission; shortly he also concurrently held the post of Vice Protector-General of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Li Linfu also took charge of the Anxi protectorate and the Shuofang command, and soon afterward the vice protectorate of Chanyu as well.

sentences.zh: 十一載，以朔方副使李獻忠叛，讓節度，舉安思順自代。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, because the Shuofang deputy commissioner Li Xianzhong rebelled, he yielded the military commission and recommended An Sishun to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the Shuofang deputy Li Xianzhong rebelled, Li Linfu relinquished the command and recommended An Sishun as his replacement.

sentences.zh: 國家武德、貞觀已來，蕃將如阿史那杜爾、契苾何力，忠孝有才略，亦不專委大將之任，多以重臣領使以制之。

translations.literal: Since Wude and Zhenguan the state, with frontier generals such as Ashina Du'er and Qibi Heli — loyal, filial, talented, and strategic — still did not solely entrust the great general's charge, but mostly had weighty ministers lead the commissions to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude and Zhenguan reigns, even frontier generals as loyal and capable as Ashina Du'er and Qibi Heli had not been given sole command. Weighty ministers at court usually held the commission posts to keep them in check.

sentences.zh: 開元中，張嘉貞、王晙、張說、蕭嵩、杜暹皆以節度使入知政事，林甫固位，誌欲杜出將入相之源，嘗奏曰：「文士為將，怯當矢石，不如用寒族、蕃人，蕃人善戰有勇，寒族即無黨援。」

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Zhang Jiazhen, Wang Jun, Zhang Yue, Xiao Song, and Du Xian all entered to handle state affairs from military commissioner posts; Linfu secured his position and resolved to block the source of generals going out and entering the chancellorship; he once memorialized: "Literary scholars as generals are timid before arrows and stones — better to use cold-clan men and frontier peoples; frontier peoples are good at battle and have courage, and cold-clan men have no factional backing.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, Zhang Jiazhen, Wang Jun, Zhang Yue, Xiao Song, and Du Xian had all risen from military commissioner posts to direct state affairs. Secure in power, Li Linfu wished to cut off the path by which frontier commanders became chancellors. He once memorialized, "When literary men serve as generals, they shrink from arrows and stones. It is better to employ men of humble birth and non-Chinese commanders. The latter are brave in battle, and the former have no factional ties.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，乃用思順代林甫領使。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded it as so and therefore used Sishun to replace Linfu in leading the commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed An Sishun to replace Li Linfu in command of the commission.

sentences.zh: 自是高仙芝、哥舒翰皆專任大將，林甫利其不識文字，無入相由，然而祿山竟為亂階，由專得大將之任故也。

translations.literal: From this Gao Xianzhi and Geshu Han were both solely entrusted as great generals; Linfu profited from their not recognizing written characters and having no path to enter the chancellorship — yet Lushan in the end became the stairway of rebellion, because of solely obtaining the great general's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Gao Xianzhi and Geshu Han held sole command as great generals. Li Linfu counted on their illiteracy and lack of any route to the chancellorship. Yet An Lushan in the end became the agent of rebellion — precisely because such men had been given sole command.

sentences.zh: 林甫恃其早達，輿馬被服，頗極鮮華。

translations.literal: Linfu relied on his early success in office; his carriages, horses, and dress were extremely bright and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu, having risen early in his career, dressed his carriages and person in the utmost splendor.

sentences.zh: 自無學術，僅能秉筆，有才名於時者尤忌之。

translations.literal: He himself had no learning; he could barely hold a brush; those with talent and reputation in the age he especially resented.
translations.idiomatic: He had no learning himself and could scarcely write; he was especially hostile to anyone with contemporary renown for talent.

sentences.zh: 而郭慎微、苑鹹文士之阘茸者，代為題尺。

translations.literal: Yet Guo Shenwei and Yuan Xian — literary men of petty incompetence — on his behalf composed letters and notes.
translations.idiomatic: Petty literati such as Guo Shenwei and Yuan Xian wrote his letters for him.

sentences.zh: 林甫典選部時，選人嚴迥判語有用「杕杜」二字者，林甫不識「杕」字，謂吏部侍郎韋陟曰：「此雲『杖杜』，何也？」

translations.literal: When Linfu presided over the Selection Bureau, a candidate Yan Tong had evaluation wording using the two characters for "didi" (the lone pear tree); Linfu did not recognize the character "di" and said to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Wei Zhi: "This says 'zhang du' (staff pear tree) — what is that?"
translations.idiomatic: While Li Linfu headed the Selection Bureau, an examiner's comment on candidate Yan Tong used the Book of Songs phrase *didi* (the lone pear tree). Not knowing the character *di*, Li Linfu asked Vice Minister of Personnel Wei Zhi, "This reads 'staff pear tree' — what does that mean?"

sentences.zh: 陟俯首不敢言。

translations.literal: Zhi bowed his head and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhi bowed his head and dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿姜度，林甫舅子，度妻誕子，林甫手書慶之曰：「聞有弄麞之慶。」

translations.literal: Jiang Du, Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Li Linfu's nephew by marriage, had a son born to his wife. Li Linfu wrote a congratulatory note in his own hand: "I hear there is the joy of playing with an elk.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Du, Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Li Linfu's nephew by marriage, had a son born to his wife. Li Linfu wrote a congratulatory note in his own hand: "I hear there is the joy of playing with an elk.

sentences.zh: 客視之掩口。

translations.literal: Guests who saw it covered their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Guests who read it covered their mouths to stifle laughter.

sentences.zh: 初，楊國忠登朝，林甫以微才不之忌；

translations.literal: At first, when Yang Guozhong entered court, Linfu because of his slight talent did not regard him with jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yang Guozhong entered court, Li Linfu did not regard this man of slight talent as a threat;

sentences.zh: 及位至中司，權傾朝列，林甫始惡之。

translations.literal: but once Yang rose to censor-in-chief and dominated the court, Li Linfu began to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: but once Yang rose to censor-in-chief and dominated the court, Li Linfu began to resent him.

sentences.zh: 時國忠兼領劍南節度，會南蠻寇邊，林甫請國忠赴鎮。

translations.literal: At that time Guozhong concurrently held the Jiannan military commission; it happened that the southern barbarians raided the border, and Linfu requested that Guozhong go to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was then also military commissioner of Jiannan. When the southern tribes raided the frontier, Li Linfu asked that Yang take up residence at his post.

sentences.zh: 帝雖依奏，然待國忠方渥，有詩送行，句末言入相之意。

translations.literal: The emperor though complying with the memorial, yet in treating Guozhong was exceedingly warm; he had a poem to send him off, and at the end of the lines expressed the intent that he enter the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request but favored Yang warmly, sending him off with a poem whose closing lines hinted that he would soon enter the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「卿止到蜀郡處置軍事，屈指待卿。」

translations.literal: It also said: "You need only go to Shu commandery to handle military affairs — I shall count the days until you return.
translations.idiomatic: It also read, "You need only go to Shu to manage military affairs; I shall count the days until you return.

sentences.zh: 林甫心尤不悅。

translations.literal: Linfu's heart was especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu's heart was especially displeased.

sentences.zh: 林甫時已寢疾。

translations.literal: Linfu at that time already lay ill in bed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was by then bedridden.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，扶疾從幸華清宮，數日增劇，巫言一見聖從差減，帝欲視之，左右諫止。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, supporting his illness he followed in attendance at Huaqing Palace; after several days his illness grew worse; shamans said that one sight of the sacred retinue would reduce it; the emperor wished to visit him; attendants remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he dragged himself along on the emperor's visit to Huaqing Palace. Within days he grew worse. Shamans said one glimpse of the imperial procession would ease him. The emperor wished to see him, but those around him dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 乃敕林甫出於庭中，上登降聖閣遙視，舉紅巾招慰之，林甫不能興，使人代拜於席。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Linfu brought out into the courtyard; the emperor ascended the Palace of Descending Sageliness and gazed from afar, raising a red cloth to wave and comfort him; Linfu could not rise and had someone bow on his behalf upon the mat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Li Linfu carried into the courtyard, then ascended the Pavilion of Descending Sageliness to look down from afar, waving a red scarf in greeting. Li Linfu could not rise and had someone bow on his behalf from his couch.

sentences.zh: 翌日，國忠自蜀還，謁林甫，拜於床下，林甫垂涕托以後事。

translations.literal: The next day Guozhong returned from Shu, visited Linfu, and bowed beneath the bed; Linfu shed tears and entrusted him with affairs thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yang Guozhong returned from Shu, visited Li Linfu, and bowed at the foot of his bed. Li Linfu wept and entrusted his affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太尉、揚州大都督，給班劍、西園秘器。

translations.literal: Before long he died; posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor, Area Commander-in-Chief of Yang Prefecture, granted court swords and secret burial vessels of the Western Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, with the grant of ceremonial guard swords and imperial burial vessels.

sentences.zh: 諸子以吉儀護柩還京師，發喪於平康坊之第。

translations.literal: His sons with auspicious rites escorted the coffin back to the capital, and the mourning was begun at his mansion in Pingkang Ward.
translations.idiomatic: His sons bore the coffin back to the capital with full honors and began the mourning rites at his mansion in Pingkang Ward.

sentences.zh: 林甫晚年溺於聲妓，姬侍盈房。

translations.literal: Linfu in his later years drowned in sound and courtesans; concubines and attendants filled the rooms.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Li Linfu drowned himself in music and courtesans; concubines filled every chamber.

sentences.zh: 自以結怨於人，常憂刺客竊發，重扃復壁，絡板甃石，一夕屢徙，雖家人不之知。

translations.literal: Because he had made enmity with men, he constantly feared assassins stealing upon him; double barred gates, layered walls, latticed boards and inlaid stone — in one night he moved many times, so that even his household did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had made many enemies, he lived in constant fear of assassins. He barred his doors, walled his chambers, and layered stone and timber defenses, moving his bed several times in a single night so that even his family did not know where he slept.

sentences.zh: 有子二十五人、女二十五人：岫為將作監，崿為司儲郎中，嶼為太常少卿；

translations.literal: He had twenty-five sons and twenty-five daughters: You was Director of the Directorate for Imperial Construction, E was Gentleman of the Bureau of Granaries, Yu was Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: He had twenty-five sons and twenty-five daughters: You was Director of Imperial Construction, E was Gentleman of the Bureau of Granaries, and Yu was Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 子婿張博濟為鴻臚少卿，鄭平為戶部員外郎，杜位為右補闕，齊宣為諫議大夫，元捴為京兆府戶曹。

translations.literal: Sons-in-law Zhang Boji was Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Receptions, Zheng Ping was Assistant Secretary of the Ministry of Revenue, Du Wei was Rectifier at the Right, Qi Xuan was Remonstrance Grandee, Yuan Cong was Revenue Clerk of the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: his sons-in-law Zhang Boji was Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Receptions, Zheng Ping was assistant secretary of the Ministry of Revenue, Du Wei was rectifier on the right, Qi Xuan was remonstrance grandee, and Yuan Cong was a revenue clerk in the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，林甫嘗夢一白晰多須長丈夫逼己，接之不能去。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Linfu once dreamed of a fair-skinned, heavily bearded, tall man pressing upon him — he could not drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Linfu dreamed of a tall, fair-skinned man with a heavy beard pressing upon him; he could not drive him away.

sentences.zh: 既寤，言曰：「此形狀類裴寬，寬謀代我故也。」

translations.literal: Upon waking he said: "This form resembles Pei Kuan — Kuan plots to replace me.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, he said, "This man looks like Pei Kuan — Kuan means to take my place.

sentences.zh: 時寬為戶部尚書、兼御史大夫，故因李適之黨斥逐之。

translations.literal: At that time Kuan was Minister of Revenue and concurrently Censor-in-Chief; therefore through Li Shizhi's faction he expelled and banished him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan was then Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief; Li Linfu used Li Shizhi's faction to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 是時楊國忠始為金吾胄曹參軍，至是不十年，林甫卒，國忠竟代其任，其形狀亦類寬焉。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Guozhong had only just been Aide of the Golden Guard Regiment; by this time not yet ten years had passed — Linfu died, Guozhong in the end replaced his post, and his form likewise resembled Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Guozhong had only begun as an aide in the Golden Guard Regiment. Less than ten years later Li Linfu died, and Yang Guozhong took his place — and his appearance too resembled Pei Kuan's.

sentences.zh: 國忠素憾林甫，既得誌，誣奏林甫與蕃將阿布思同構逆謀，誘林甫親族間素不悅者為之證。

translations.literal: Guozhong had long resented Linfu; having obtained his wish, he falsely memorialized that Linfu with the frontier general Abu Si jointly plotted rebellion, enticing among Linfu's kinsmen those who were not pleased with him to testify.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong had long hated Li Linfu. Once in power, he falsely accused him of plotting rebellion with the Tangut general Abu Si and induced discontented members of Li Linfu's clan to testify.

sentences.zh: 詔奪林甫官爵，廢為庶人，岫、崿諸子並謫於嶺表。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Linfu's offices and enfeoffment and demoted him to commoner; You, E, and the other sons were all exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Li Linfu of rank and made him a commoner. You, E, and the other sons were exiled to the south.

sentences.zh: 林甫性沈密，城府深阻，未嘗以愛憎見於容色。

translations.literal: Linfu's nature was deep and secret; his inner chambers profoundly obstructed; he never let love or hate show on his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was secretive by nature, with schemes beyond measure, and never let love or hatred show on his face.

sentences.zh: 自處臺衡，動循格令，衣寇士子，非常調無仕進之門。

translations.literal: From the time he stood at the balance of the terrace, his movements followed regulations and statutes; garbed in the scholar's robe, without the regular route there was no gate of official advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the chancellorship, he kept to the rules, wore scholar's dress, and barred advancement to anyone outside the regular examination track.

sentences.zh: 所以秉鈞二十年，朝野側目，憚其威權。

translations.literal: Because of this he held the scale for twenty years; court and countryside looked askance, in awe of his majestic power.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he wielded power for twenty years while court and countryside looked on in fear of his might.

sentences.zh: 及國忠誣構，天下以為冤。

translations.literal: When Guozhong falsely framed him, the realm regarded it as injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong framed him, the realm regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠，本名釗，蒲州永樂人也。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong, whose original name was Zhao, was from Yongle in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, whose original name was Zhao, was from Yongle in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父珣，以國忠貴，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Xun, because Guozhong became noble, was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun was posthumously made Minister of War when Yang Guozhong rose to power.

sentences.zh: 則天朝幸臣張易之，即國忠之舅也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi, a favored minister in Empress Wu's court, was precisely Guozhong's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi, a favorite of Empress Wu, was his maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 國忠無學術拘檢，能飲酒，蒱博無行，為宗黨所鄙。

translations.literal: Guozhong had no learning or restraint; he could drink wine and was unrestrained at gambling — the lineage scorned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong had no learning or self-restraint. He drank heavily, gambled without shame, and was despised by his clan.

sentences.zh: 乃發憤從軍，事蜀帥，以屯優當遷，益州長史張寬惡其為人，因事笞之，竟以屯優授新都尉。

translations.literal: He then in indignation joined the army, serving the Shu commander; because of excellence in garrison field he should have been promoted — the Administrator of Yizhou Zhang Kuan hated his character and on a pretext flogged him, yet in the end because of garrison excellence appointed him Magistrate of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He left in anger to join the army under the Shu commander. Though marked for promotion for his record in the garrison forces, Zhang Kuan, prefectural administrator of Yizhou, detested his character and had him flogged on a pretext, yet in the end appointed him magistrate of Xindu because of his garrison record.

sentences.zh: 稍遷金吾衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Military Staff Officer of the Golden Guard Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to military staff officer of the Golden Guard Regiment.

sentences.zh: 太真妃，即國忠從祖妹也。

translations.literal: Consort Taizhen was precisely Guozhong's cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Taizhen — Yang Guifei — was his cousin on the father's side.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，太真有寵，劍南節度使章仇兼瓊引國忠為賓佐，既而擢授監察御史。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era Taizhen had favor; the Jiannan Military Commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong brought Guozhong in as a guest staff officer, and before long elevated and appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era, when Yang Guifei was favored, the Jiannan commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong took Yang Guozhong on staff and soon had him made supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 去就輕率，驟履清貴，朝士指目嗤之。

translations.literal: His coming and going were frivolous; he suddenly tread the pure and honored stations — court gentlemen pointed and jeered.
translations.idiomatic: His comings and goings were frivolous. Thrust suddenly into high office, courtiers pointed and laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 時李林甫將不利於皇太子，掎摭陰事以傾之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Linfu was about to act against the Crown Prince, gathering secret matters to topple him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was then plotting against the Crown Prince, gathering secret evidence to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 侍御史楊慎矜承望風旨，誣太子妃兄韋堅與皇甫惟明私謁太子，以國忠怙寵敢言，援之為黨，以按其事。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Yang Shenjin received and followed the intent of the wind, falsely accusing the Crown Prince's consort's elder brother Wei Jian and Huangfu Weiming of privately visiting the Crown Prince; because Guozhong relied on favor and dared speak, he drew him into a faction to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Yang Shenjin took his cue from this wind. He falsely accused the Crown Prince's brother-in-law Wei Jian and Huangfu Weiming of visiting the Crown Prince in secret. Yang Guozhong, emboldened by imperial favor, joined the faction to prosecute the case.

sentences.zh: 京兆府法曹吉溫舞文巧詆，為國忠爪牙之用，因深竟堅獄，堅及太子良娣杜氏、親屬柳勣、杜昆吾等，痛繩其罪，以樹威權。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefecture Legal Clerk Ji Wen twisted documents and cunningly slandered, used as Guozhong's claw and fang; thereby deeply concluding Jian's prison case — Jian and the Crown Prince's honored consort Lady Du, kinsmen Liu Ji, Du Kunwu, and others were harshly bound in guilt to plant majestic power.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen of the metropolitan legal bureau twisted statutes to defame them and served as Yang Guozhong's enforcer. The case against Wei Jian was pressed to the hilt; Wei Jian, the Crown Prince's honored consort Lady Du, and kinsmen Liu Ji and Du Kunwu were punished severely to build Yang's power.

sentences.zh: 於京城別置推院，自是連歲大獄，追捕擠陷，誅夷者數百家，皆國忠發之。

translations.literal: In the capital a separate interrogation court was established; from this year after year great prisons, pursuit, crowding, and framing — those exterminated numbered several hundred houses, all initiated by Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: A separate interrogation court was set up in the capital. Year after year great trials followed, with pursuit, entrapment, and executions wiping out hundreds of families — all at Yang Guozhong's instigation.

sentences.zh: 林甫方深阻保位，國忠凡所奏劾，涉疑似於太子者，林甫雖不明言以指導之，皆林甫所使，國忠乘而為邪，得以肆意。

translations.literal: Linfu was then deeply blocking to preserve his position; whatever Guozhong memorialized in impeachment touching suspicion of the Crown Prince — though Linfu did not openly speak to guide it, all were sent by Linfu; Guozhong rode it to do evil and could act as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was guarding his position through obstruction. Every impeachment Yang Guozhong filed that touched the Crown Prince, though Li Linfu did not openly direct him, came at Li Linfu's bidding. Yang Guozhong rode that current to do evil as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 上春秋高，意有所愛惡，國忠探知其情，動契所欲。

translations.literal: The emperor's years were advanced; his mind had loves and hates; Guozhong probed and knew his disposition, and in movement matched what he desired.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was advanced in years with shifting likes and dislikes. Yang Guozhong read his moods and shaped his actions to match them.

sentences.zh: 驟遷檢校度支員外郎，兼侍御史，監水陸運及司農、出納錢物、內中市買、召募劍南健兒等使。

translations.literal: He was suddenly promoted Acting Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently Attending Censor, supervising water and land transport and the ministries of agriculture, receipts and disbursements of goods and coin, inner-palace market purchases, recruiting hardy men of Jiannan, and other commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He was swiftly made acting assistant in the Ministry of Revenue and concurrent attending censor, with charge of water and land transport, state granaries, treasury disbursements, inner-palace purchases, recruitment of Jiannan troops, and other duties.

sentences.zh: 以稱職遷度支郎中，不期年，兼領十五餘使，轉給事中、兼御史中丞，專判度支事。

translations.literal: Because of competent performance he was promoted Gentleman in the Ministry of Revenue; before a year's span he concurrently held more than fifteen commissions, was transferred to Palace Recepient, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and solely decided Revenue Ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For competent service he was made gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue. Within a year he held more than fifteen commissions, became palace recepient and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and took sole charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲，貴妃姊虢國、韓國、秦國三夫人同日拜命，兄銛拜鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: That year the consort's elder sisters the Ladies of Guo State, Han State, and Qin State received appointments on the same day; elder brother Qian was appointed Director of the Court for Diplomatic Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: That year the consort's sisters, the Ladies of Guo, Han, and Qin states, were ennobled on the same day, and her brother Qian was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Receptions.

sentences.zh: 八載，玄宗召公卿百僚觀左藏庫，喜其貨幣山積，面賜國忠金紫，兼權太府卿事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Emperor Xuanzong summoned dukes and ministers and the hundred officials to view the Left Vault; pleased that currency and goods piled like mountains, he personally granted Guozhong gold and purple, and concurrently acting charge of the Grand Vault Director's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Emperor Xuanzong summoned officials to view the Left Vault and, pleased that treasure piled like mountains, personally granted Yang Guozhong the gold-and-purple insignia and acting charge of the Grand Vault.

sentences.zh: 國忠既專錢谷之任，出入禁中，日加親幸。

translations.literal: Guozhong having monopolized the charge of coin and grain, entering and leaving the forbidden precincts, day by day grew in intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Guozhong controlled finance, his comings and goings in the palace won him greater favor day by day.

sentences.zh: 初，楊慎矜希林甫旨，引王鉷為御史中丞，同構大獄，以傾東宮。

translations.literal: At first Yang Shenjin hoped for Linfu's intent, brought in Wang Hong as Vice Censor-in-Chief, and together framed a great prison case to topple the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yang Shenjin courted Li Linfu's favor, brought in Wang Hong as vice censor-in-chief, and together framed a great case to destroy the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 既帝意不回，慎矜稍避事防患，因與鉷有隙。

translations.literal: Since the emperor's intent did not turn back, Shenjin gradually avoided affairs to guard against harm, and thereby had a rift with Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's mind did not change, Yang Shenjin grew cautious and fell out with Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 鉷乃附國忠，奏誣慎矜，誅其昆仲，由是權傾內外，公卿惕息。

translations.literal: Hong then attached to Guozhong, memorialized to falsely accuse Shenjin, executed his brothers, and from this power tipped inside and outside — dukes and ministers trembled and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong then attached himself to Yang Guozhong, falsely accused Yang Shenjin, and had his brothers executed. Thereafter power tilted entirely toward Yang Guozhong, and officials trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 吉溫為國忠陳移奪執政之策，國忠用其謀，尋兼兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Ji Wen for Guozhong set forth the strategy of displacing and seizing the chancellorship; Guozhong used his plan, and before long concurrently held Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen outlined for Yang Guozhong a plan to seize the chancellorship. Yang Guozhong adopted it and soon became vice minister of war as well.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹蕭炅、御史中丞宋渾皆林甫所親善，國忠皆誣奏譴逐，林甫不能救。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Xiao Jiong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Hun were all those Linfu favored; Guozhong in each case falsely memorialized to condemn and banish them — Linfu could not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan governor Xiao Jiong and vice censor-in-chief Song Hun were both favorites of Li Linfu. Yang Guozhong falsely accused each and had them banished; Li Linfu could not save them.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為御史大夫，兼京兆尹，恩寵侔於國忠，而位望居其右。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Metropolitan Governor; imperial favor matched Guozhong's, yet in position and prestige he stood to his right.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was censor-in-chief and concurrent metropolitan governor. His favor rivaled Yang Guozhong's, and his rank stood above Yang's.

sentences.zh: 國忠忌其與己分權，會邢縡事泄，乃陷鉷兄弟誅之，因代鉷為御史大夫，權京兆尹，賜名國忠。

translations.literal: Guozhong resented that he shared power with him; it happened that Xing Zong's affair leaked out — he then framed Hong and his brother and executed them, and thereby replaced Hong as Censor-in-Chief, acting Metropolitan Governor, and was granted the name Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong resented Wang Hong's share of power. When Xing Zong's plot was exposed, he framed Wang Hong and his brother and had them executed, then took Wang's posts as censor-in-chief and acting metropolitan governor and was granted the name Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 乃窮竟邢縡獄，令引林甫交私鉷、銲與阿布思事狀，而陳希烈、哥舒翰附會國忠，證成其狀，上由是疏薄林甫。

translations.literal: He then pressed the Xing Zong case to the end, extracting testimony that Li Linfu had secret dealings with Wang Hong, Wang Han, and Abu Si. Chen Xilie and Geshu Han backed Yang Guozhong's case and confirmed the charges, and the emperor thereafter grew cool toward Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed the Xing Zong case to the end, extracting testimony that Li Linfu had secret dealings with Wang Hong, Wang Han, and Abu Si. Chen Xilie and Geshu Han backed Yang Guozhong's case and confirmed the charges, and the emperor thereafter grew cool toward Li Linfu.

sentences.zh: 南蠻質子閤羅鳳亡歸不獲，帝怒甚，欲討之。

translations.literal: The southern barbarian hostage Geluofeng fled home and could not be recovered; the emperor was very angry and wished to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The southern tribal hostage Geluofeng fled home and could not be recaptured. The emperor was furious and wished to punish him.

sentences.zh: 國忠薦閬州人鮮于仲通為益州長史，令率精兵八萬討南蠻，與羅鳳戰於瀘南，全軍陷沒。

translations.literal: Guozhong recommended Xianyu Zhongtong of Lang Prefecture as Administrator of Yizhou, ordering him to lead eighty thousand picked troops to campaign against the southern barbarians; he fought Geluofeng south of Lu — the entire army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong recommended Xianyu Zhongtong of Langzhou as administrator of Yizhou and sent him with eighty thousand elite troops against the southern tribes. He fought Geluofeng south of Lu, and the entire army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 國忠掩其敗狀，仍敘其戰功，仍令仲通上表請國忠兼領益部。

translations.literal: Guozhong concealed the defeat and still narrated his battle merit, and still had Zhongtong memorialize requesting that Guozhong concurrently hold the Yi region.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong concealed the defeat, still reported it as a victory, and had Zhongtong memorialize asking that Yang Guozhong be given concurrent command of Yizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 十載，國忠權知蜀郡都督府長史，充劍南節度副大使，知節度事，仍薦仲通代己為京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Guozhong acting knew the Chief Administrator of the Shu Commandery Governor's Office, filled the post of Jiannan Deputy Military Commissioner, knew military commission affairs, and still recommended Zhongtong to replace himself as Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Yang Guozhong was acting chief administrator of the Shu commandery, deputy military commissioner of Jiannan with full authority, and recommended Zhongtong to replace him as metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 國忠又使司馬李宓率師七萬再討南蠻。

translations.literal: Guozhong again had Staff Officer Li Mi lead an army of seventy thousand to campaign again against the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong then sent staff officer Li Mi with seventy thousand men on a second campaign against the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 宓渡瀘水，為蠻所誘，至和城，不戰而敗，李宓死於陣。

translations.literal: Mi crossed the Lu River, was lured by the barbarians to He City, was defeated without battle, and Li Mi died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi crossed the Lu River, was lured by the tribes to He City, was routed without a fight, and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 國忠又隱其敗，以捷書上聞。

translations.literal: Guozhong again concealed the defeat and reported victory to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong again concealed the defeat and reported a victory to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自仲通、李宓再舉討蠻之軍，其征發皆中國利兵，然於土風不便，沮洳之所陷，瘴疫之所傷，饋餉之所乏，物故者十八九。

translations.literal: From Zhongtong and Li Mi raising twice the armies to campaign against the barbarians, their levies were all China's sharp troops — yet they were ill-suited to local custom, mired in boggy ground, harmed by miasmic pestilence, short of provisions — those who perished were eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: From the two campaigns led by Zhongtong and Li Mi, every levy drew China's finest troops, yet they were unsuited to the terrain, mired in bogs, stricken by pestilence, and starved of supplies. Eight or nine in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 凡舉二十萬眾，棄之死地，只輪不還，人銜冤毒，無敢言者。

translations.literal: In all they raised two hundred thousand men, abandoned them in the land of death — not even a wheel returned; men bore grievance and poison, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In all, two hundred thousand men were raised and abandoned to die; not even a cart wheel came back. The people nursed bitter grievances, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 國忠尋兼山南西道采訪使。

translations.literal: Guozhong before long concurrently held the post of Investigation Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong soon became investigation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit as well.

sentences.zh: 十一載，南蠻侵蜀，蜀人請國忠赴鎮，林甫亦奏遣之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the southern barbarians invaded Shu; the people of Shu requested that Guozhong go to the commandery, and Linfu also memorialized to send him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the southern tribes invaded Shu. The people of Shu asked that Yang Guozhong take command, and Li Linfu memorialized to send him there.

sentences.zh: 將辭，雨泣懇陳必為林甫所排，帝憐之，不數月召還。

translations.literal: About to take leave, weeping in rain he earnestly stated that he would surely be pushed aside by Linfu; the emperor pitied him, and within not several months summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, he wept and pleaded that Li Linfu would surely destroy him. The emperor pitied him and recalled him within a few months.

sentences.zh: 會林甫卒，遂代為右相，兼吏部尚書、集賢殿大學士、太清太微宮使、判度支、劍南節度、山南西道采訪、兩京出納租庸鑄錢等使並如故。

translations.literal: It happened that Linfu died; he then replaced him as Right Chancellor, concurrently Minister of Personnel, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Commissioner of the Palaces of Great Clarity and Supreme Subtlety, deciding Revenue affairs, Jiannan military commission, Shannan West investigation, and the two capitals' receipt and disbursement of land tax, corvée substitution, and coin casting — all as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu died, Yang Guozhong succeeded him as right chancellor, retaining his posts as minister of personnel, grand academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, commissioner of the imperial palaces, controller of revenue, military commissioner of Jiannan, investigation commissioner of Shannan West, and supervisor of tax and coinage affairs in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 國忠本性疏躁，強力有口辯，既以便佞得宰相，剖決機務，居之不疑。

translations.literal: Guozhong by nature was loose and rash, forceful and skilled in oral disputation; having by fawning flattery obtained the chancellorship, he sliced and decided urgent affairs, occupying it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was by nature rash and impulsive, forceful and glib. Having reached the chancellorship through flattery, he settled state affairs without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 立朝之際，或攘袂扼腕，自公卿已下，皆頤指氣使，無不詟憚。

translations.literal: When standing at court he would sometimes push up his sleeves and clutch his wrist; from dukes and ministers downward, all were commanded by chin and breath — none did not tremble in awe.
translations.idiomatic: In court he would roll up his sleeves and clench his fists. From dukes and ministers downward, all obeyed his gestures and tone, and none did not fear him.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相居臺輔之地，以元功盛德居之，不務威權，出入騎從簡易。

translations.literal: By precedent, the chancellor occupied the terrace-assist post with founding merit and great virtue; he did not pursue majestic power; going out and in, mounted escort was simple.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the chancellor held his post through founding merit and great virtue, did not pursue displays of power, and traveled with a modest escort.

sentences.zh: 自林甫承恩顧年深，每出車騎滿街，節將、侍郎有所關白，皆趨走辟易，有同案吏。

translations.literal: From the time Linfu received favor and regard for many years, each time he went out carriages and horses filled the streets; military commissioners and vice ministers who had matters to report all ran and gave way, like desk clerks.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Li Linfu had long enjoyed imperial favor, his processions filled the streets. Military commissioners and vice ministers who wished to petition him all ran to give way, like clerks before a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 舊例，宰相午後六刻始出歸第，林甫奏太平無事，以巳時還第，機務填委，皆決於私家。

translations.literal: Old precedent: the chancellor only left to return to his mansion after the sixth quarter of the afternoon; Linfu memorialized that all under Heaven was peaceful and without affair, and returned to his mansion at the si hour; urgent affairs piled up — all were decided in his private home.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom the chancellor left office only in late afternoon. Li Linfu reported that the realm was at peace and returned home at mid-morning; pressing affairs were all decided at his private residence.

sentences.zh: 主書吳珣持籍就左相陳希烈之第，希烈引籍署名，都無可否。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wu Xun took the register to Left Chancellor Chen Xilie's mansion; Xilie drew out the register and signed his name — entirely without approval or denial.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Wu Xun brought the register to Left Chancellor Chen Xilie's house. Chen Xilie merely signed it without approving or rejecting anything.

sentences.zh: 國忠代之，亦如前政。

translations.literal: Guozhong replaced him and likewise followed the previous administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong succeeded him and governed in the same way.

sentences.zh: 國忠自侍御史以至宰相，凡領四十餘使，又專判度支、吏部三銓，事務鞅掌，但署一字，猶不能盡，皆責成胥吏，賄賂公行。

translations.literal: Guozhong from Attending Censor to chancellor in all held more than forty commissions, and again solely decided Revenue and the three selections of the Ministry of Personnel; affairs were abundant — even to sign one character he still could not finish all, and all were charged to clerks; bribes walked openly.
translations.idiomatic: From attending censor to chancellor, Yang Guozhong held more than forty commissions and personally controlled revenue and all three personnel selections. Affairs were so numerous that he could not even sign his name to everything and left it all to clerks, while bribes flowed openly.

sentences.zh: 國忠既以宰臣典選，奏請銓日便定留放，不用長名。

translations.literal: Guozhong having as chancellor minister presided over selection, memorialized requesting that on selection day retention and release be fixed at once, not using the long register.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor in charge of appointments, Yang Guozhong memorialized that candidates be approved or rejected on the day of selection, dispensing with the long register.

sentences.zh: 先天已前，諸司官知政事，午後歸本司決事，兵部尚書、侍郎亦分銓註擬。

translations.literal: Before the Xiantian era, officials of various bureaus who knew state affairs returned to their bureaus in the afternoon to decide affairs; the Minister of War and Vice Ministers also divided selection and drafted appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Xiantian era, officials who handled state affairs returned to their ministries in the afternoon to decide business, and the minister and vice ministers of war also shared in drafting appointments.

sentences.zh: 開元已後，宰臣數少，始崇其任，不歸本司。

translations.literal: After the Kaiyuan era the number of chancellor ministers was few; they first exalted the charge and did not return to their bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan, with fewer chancellors, the post grew more exalted and they no longer returned to their original ministries.

sentences.zh: 故事，吏部三銓，三註三唱，自春及夏，才終其事。

translations.literal: By precedent the Ministry of Personnel's three selections required three draftings and three announcements; from spring to summer the affair was only then finished.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Ministry of Personnel's three selection boards required three rounds of drafting and announcement, and the process ran from spring into summer before it was done.

sentences.zh: 國忠使胥吏於私第暗定官員，集百僚於尚書省對註唱，一日令畢，以誇神速，資格差謬，無復倫序。

translations.literal: Guozhong had clerks at his private mansion secretly fix officials, gathered the hundred officials at the Ministry of Personnel for facing register and announcement, and in one day ordered it finished to boast of divine speed — qualifications were wrong and confused, and there was no longer order of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong had clerks secretly fix appointments at his mansion, then gathered officials at the Ministry of Personnel to announce them in a single day to boast of his speed. Qualifications were confused and proper order was lost.

sentences.zh: 明年註擬，又於私第大集選人，令諸女弟垂簾觀之，笑語之聲，朗聞於外。

translations.literal: The next year in drafting appointments, again at his private mansion he greatly gathered candidates, ordered his various younger sisters to hang curtains and watch — the sound of laughter and talk clearly heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when drafting appointments, he again gathered candidates at his mansion and had his sisters watch from behind curtains; their laughter was clearly heard outside.

sentences.zh: 故事，註官訖，過門下侍中、給事中。

translations.literal: By precedent, when registering officials was finished, it passed the Palace Secretariat's Attendant-in-Chief and Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, after officials were registered, the list passed through the Palace Secretariat to the attendant-in-chief and drafting attendants.

sentences.zh: 國忠註官時，呼左相陳希烈於座隅，給事中在列，曰：「既對註擬，過門下了矣。」

translations.literal: When Guozhong registered officials, he called Left Chancellor Chen Xilie to a corner of the seat; Drafting Attendants were in the ranks; he said: "Since we have faced the register and drafted, it has already passed the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong registered officials, he called Left Chancellor Chen Xilie to one side while drafting attendants stood by and said, "Since we have announced the appointments here, they have already passed through the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎韋見素、張倚皆衣紫，是日與本曹郎官同咨事，趨走於屏樹之間。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers of Personnel Wei Jiansu and Zhang Yi both wore purple; that day together with the gentlemen of their bureau they consulted on affairs, hurrying and running among screens and trees.
translations.idiomatic: Vice ministers of personnel Wei Jiansu and Zhang Yi, both in purple robes, that day consulted on business alongside their bureau gentlemen, hurrying among the screens and trees.

sentences.zh: 既退，國忠謂諸妹曰：「兩員紫袍主事何如人？」

translations.literal: After they withdrew, Guozhong said to his various younger sisters: "Those two purple-robed chief administrators — what sort of men are they?
translations.idiomatic: After they left, Yang Guozhong said to his sisters, "What do you think of those two purple-robed chiefs of office?

sentences.zh: 相對大噱。

translations.literal: Facing one another they laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: They looked at one another and burst into loud laughter.

sentences.zh: 其所昵京兆尹鮮于仲通、中書舍人竇華、侍御史鄭昂諷選人於省門立碑，以頌國忠銓綜之能。

translations.literal: Those he favored — Metropolitan Governor Xianyu Zhongtong, Palace Drafting Attendant Dou Hua, Attending Censor Zheng Ang — prompted candidates at the ministry gate to erect a stele praising Guozhong's ability in selection and synthesis.
