translations.idiomatic: His favorites — metropolitan governor Xianyu Zhongtong, palace drafting attendant Dou Hua, and attending censor Zheng Ang — induced candidates to erect a stele at the ministry gate praising Yang Guozhong's skill in appointments.

sentences.zh: 貴妃姊虢國夫人，國忠與之私，於宣義裏構連甲第，土木被綈繡，棟宇之盛，兩都莫比，晝會夜集，無復禮度。

translations.literal: The consort's elder sister the Lady of Guo State — Guozhong had a private affair with her; in Xuanyi Ward they built linked mansions of the first rank; earth and wood were covered in silk brocade; the splendor of beams and rafters — neither capital could compare; by day they met, by night they gathered — no longer any ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong had an affair with the consort's sister, the Lady of Guo State. In Xuanyi Ward they built linked mansions draped in brocade, whose grandeur neither capital could match. They held revels day and night without regard for propriety.

sentences.zh: 有時與虢國並轡入朝，揮鞭走馬，以為諧謔，衢路觀之，無不駭嘆。

translations.literal: Sometimes together with the Lady of Guo they entered court side by side on the reins, whipping and racing horses as jest — those who watched on the thoroughfare all were startled and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he and the Lady of Guo rode side by side into court, whipping their horses in jest. Passersby on the streets were all shocked and amazed.

sentences.zh: 玄宗每年冬十月幸華清宮，常經冬還宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong every year in the tenth month of winter visited Huaqing Palace and commonly passed the winter before returning to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Every year in the tenth month Emperor Xuanzong visited Huaqing Palace and usually stayed through the winter before returning.

sentences.zh: 國忠山第在宮東門之南，與虢國相對，韓國、秦國甍棟相接，天子幸其第，必過五家，賞賜宴樂。

translations.literal: Guozhong's mountain mansion was south of the palace's eastern gate, facing the Lady of Guo; the Ladies of Han and Qin had ridgepoles and beams touching; when the Son of Heaven visited their mansions, he must pass all five households — rewards, feasts, and music.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong's hill mansion stood south of the palace's eastern gate, facing the Lady of Guo's residence, with the Ladies of Han and Qin adjoining. When the emperor visited, he passed all five households in turn, bestowing rewards and feasts.

sentences.zh: 每扈從驪山，五家合隊，國忠以劍南幢節引於前，出有餞路，還有軟腳，遠近餉遺，珍玩狗馬，閹侍歌兒，相望於道。

translations.literal: Each time escorting to Mount Li, the five households formed a combined procession; Guozhong with Jiannan banners and insignia led in front; going out there were farewell feasts on the road, returning there were escort relays — near and far sent gifts: rare objects, dogs, horses, eunuch attendants, singing boys — gazing at one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they escorted the emperor to Mount Li, the five households marched together, with Yang Guozhong leading under his Jiannan banners. Farewell feasts lined the road going out, and relay escorts on the return. Gifts of treasure, horses, eunuchs, and singing boys streamed along the route from far and near.

sentences.zh: 進封衛國公，食實封三百戶，俄拜司空。

translations.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Wei State, with three hundred households of substantive fief; before long he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Wei with a substantive fief of three hundred households, and soon after was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時安祿山恩寵特深，總握兵柄，國忠知其跋扈，終不出其下，將圖之，屢於上前言其悖逆之狀，上不之信。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan enjoyed favor exceptionally deep, grasping overall military authority; Guozhong knew his overbearing manner, that in the end he would not rank below him, and intended to plot against him; repeatedly before the sovereign he spoke of his rebellious conduct, but the sovereign did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan then stood in extraordinary imperial favor and held all military power. Yang Guozhong knew his arrogance and that he would never accept subordination; Guozhong meant to destroy him and repeatedly warned the emperor of treason, but Xuanzong would not believe him.

sentences.zh: 是時，祿山已專制河北，聚幽、并勁騎，陰圖逆節，動未有名，伺上千秋萬歲之後，方圖叛換。

translations.literal: At that time Lushan already monopolized Hebei, gathered elite cavalry of You and Bing, secretly plotted treasonous design; his movement had not yet a name, waiting until after the sovereign's thousand autumns and ten thousand years, only then plotting rebellion and change.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lushan already ruled Hebei alone, mustered crack horsemen from You and Bing, and secretly planned revolt. He had not yet moved openly, biding his time until the emperor's death before turning traitor.

sentences.zh: 及見國忠用事，慮不利於己，祿山遙領內外閑廄使，遂以兵部侍郎吉溫知留後，兼御史中丞、京畿采訪使，內伺朝廷動靜。

translations.literal: When he saw Guozhong wield affairs, fearing harm to himself, Lushan held at a distance the post of Commissioner of Internal and External Studs; then he made Vice Minister of War Ji Wen know the acting command, also Vice Censor-in-Chief and Capital Region Investigation Commissioner, inwardly spying on court movements.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Guozhong in power and feared for himself, Lushan retained the distant title of Commissioner of the Imperial Studs, appointed Ji Wen of the Ministry of War as acting commander with concurrent posts as vice censor and capital investigator, and used him to watch the court from within.

sentences.zh: 國忠使門客蹇昂、何盈求祿山陰事，圍捕其宅，得李超、安岱等，使侍御史鄭昂縊殺於御史臺。

translations.literal: Guozhong sent retainers Jian Ang and He Ying to seek Lushan's secret affairs, surrounded and seized his residence, obtained Li Chao, An Dai and others, and had Attending Censor Zheng Ang strangle them at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong sent his clients Jian Ang and He Ying to uncover Lushan's secrets, surrounded his house, seized Li Chao, An Dai, and others, and had the censor Zheng Ang strangle them in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 又奏貶吉溫於合浦，以激怒祿山，幸其搖動，內以取信於上，上竟不之悟。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to demote Ji Wen to Hepu, to provoke Lushan's anger, hoping he would be shaken; inwardly to win the sovereign's trust — yet the sovereign in the end did not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Ji Wen banished to Hepu to goad Lushan, hoping to unsettle him while winning the emperor's trust inwardly. Xuanzong never saw through it.

sentences.zh: 由是祿山惶懼，遂舉兵以誅國忠為名。

translations.literal: Because of this Lushan grew fearful and alarmed, and then raised troops under the name of executing Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan, now afraid, raised his armies under the banner of punishing Yang Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞河朔變起，欲以皇太子監國，自欲親征，謀於國忠。

translations.literal: Xuanzong heard rebellion rise in the Hebei region, wished to have the crown prince supervise the state, himself wished to campaign in person, and took counsel with Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong heard of the uprising in Hebei, he planned to leave the crown prince as regent and lead the campaign himself, and consulted Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 國忠大懼，歸謂姊妹曰：「我等死在旦夕。

translations.literal: Guozhong was greatly afraid; returning home he said to his sisters: "We shall die within days.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was terrified. He went home and told his sisters, "We are as good as dead.

sentences.zh: 今東宮監國，當與娘子等並命矣。」

translations.literal: If now the Eastern Palace supervises the state, we shall share fate with you ladies and all.
translations.idiomatic: If the crown prince becomes regent now, we and you ladies will perish together.

sentences.zh: 姊妹哭訴於貴妃，貴妃銜土請命，其事乃止。

translations.literal: The sisters wept and pleaded before the Noble Consort; the Noble Consort held earth in her mouth and begged for their lives, and the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: His sisters wept before the Noble Consort, who pleaded with earth in her mouth until the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及哥舒翰守潼關，諸將以函關距京師三百里，利在守險，不利出攻。

translations.literal: When Geshu Han guarded Tong Pass, the generals said that Hanguan was three hundred li from the capital — the advantage lay in holding the defiles, not in sallying forth to attack.
translations.idiomatic: While Geshu Han held Tong Pass, his officers argued that the pass stood three hundred li from the capital: the wise course was to hold the terrain, not to attack.

sentences.zh: 國忠以翰持兵未決，慮反圖己，欲其速戰，自中督促之。

translations.literal: Guozhong, because Han held troops yet was undecided, feared he would turn and plot against him, wanted him to fight quickly, and from the center urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong feared that Han, holding the army but hesitating, might turn on him, and pressed from court for a swift battle.

sentences.zh: 翰不獲已出關，及接戰桃林，王師奔敗，哥舒受擒，敗國喪師，皆國忠之誤惑也。

translations.literal: Han, unable to refuse, marched out of the pass; when battle was joined at Taolin the royal army fled in defeat, Geshu was captured — the ruined state and lost army were all Guozhong's delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Han could not refuse and marched out; at Taolin the imperial army was routed and Geshu Han taken. The lost war was Guozhong's doing.

sentences.zh: 自祿山兵起，國忠以身領劍南節制，乃布置腹心於梁、益間，以圖自全之計。

translations.literal: From the time Lushan's troops rose, Guozhong personally led the Jiannan defense command, and deployed trusted men between Liang and Yi to plot a plan for his own preservation.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan rebelled, Guozhong took personal command of Jiannan and planted his own men between Liang and Yi to secure an escape.

sentences.zh: 六月九日，潼關不守。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the sixth month Tong Pass could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of the sixth month, Tong Pass fell.

sentences.zh: 十二日淩晨，上率龍武將軍陳玄禮、左相韋見素、京兆尹魏方進，國忠與貴妃及親屬，擁上出延秋門，諸王妃主從之不及，慮賊奄至，令內侍曹大仙擊鼓於春明門外，又焚芻槁之積，煙火燭天。

translations.literal: In the early hours of the twelfth day the sovereign led Dragon Martial General Chen Xuanli, Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu, Metropolitan Governor Wei Fangjin, Guozhong and the Noble Consort and kin, escorting the sovereign out through Yanqiu Gate; various princes' wives and princesses could not keep up; fearing the rebels would suddenly arrive, he ordered eunuch Cao Daxian to beat drums outside Chunming Gate, and also burned stacks of fodder — smoke and flames lit the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn on the twelfth the emperor fled through Yanqiu Gate with Chen Xuanli, Wei Jiansu, Wei Fangjin, Guozhong, the Noble Consort, and their kin. Princesses and consorts were left behind. To delay pursuit he had drums beaten at Chunming Gate and fodder stores burned until the sky blazed.

sentences.zh: 既渡渭，即令斷便橋。

translations.literal: Having crossed the Wei, he immediately ordered the pontoon bridge cut.
translations.idiomatic: Once across the Wei River, he ordered the floating bridge destroyed.

sentences.zh: 辰時，至咸陽望賢驛，官吏駭竄，無復貴賤，坐宮門大樹下。

translations.literal: At the chen hour they reached Wangxian post station at Xianyang; officials fled in terror; noble and common alike were gone; they sat beneath the great tree of the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-morning they reached Wangxian Station at Xianyang. Officials had fled in panic; no one of rank or low degree remained. The court sat under the great tree by the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 亭午，上猶未食，有老父獻麥，帝令具飯，始得食。

translations.literal: At midday the sovereign had still not eaten; an old man presented wheat; the emperor ordered a meal prepared and only then ate.
translations.idiomatic: At noon the emperor had still not eaten. An old man brought wheat; only then was a meal prepared and he was fed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，至馬嵬，軍士饑而憤怒，龍武將軍陳玄禮懼亂，先謂軍士曰：「今天下崩離，萬乘震蕩，豈不由楊國忠割剝氓庶，朝野怨咨，以至此耶？

translations.literal: The next day they reached Mawei; the soldiers were hungry and angry; Dragon Martial General Chen Xuanli feared disorder and first addressed the soldiers: "Today the realm is torn asunder and the imperial carriage shaken — is it not because Yang Guozhong stripped the common folk, provoking resentment throughout court and countryside, that we have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: The next day at Mawei the troops were hungry and furious. Chen Xuanli, fearing mutiny, spoke to them first: "The realm is breaking apart and the throne shaken. Is this not because Yang Guozhong preyed on the people until court and countryside boiled with hate?

sentences.zh: 若不誅之以謝天下，何以塞四海之怨憤！」

translations.literal: If we do not execute him to answer to the realm, how can we satisfy the resentment and rage of the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: If we do not kill him to answer the world, how can we quiet the fury of the empire?

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「念之久矣。

translations.literal: The crowd said: "We have long thought on this.
translations.idiomatic: The men cried, "We have wanted this for a long time.

sentences.zh: 事行，身死固所願也。」

translations.literal: If the deed is done, death itself is what we wish.
translations.idiomatic: If it is done, we are content to die.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃和好使在驛門遮國忠訴事，軍士呼曰：「楊國忠與蕃人謀叛。」

translations.literal: It happened that Tibetan envoys for peaceful relations were at the post gate blocking Guozhong to present a grievance; the soldiers shouted: "Yang Guozhong is plotting rebellion with the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Tibetan envoys at the gate were pleading with Guozhong. The soldiers shouted, "Yang Guozhong is plotting rebellion with the foreigners."

sentences.zh: 諸軍乃圍驛擒國忠，斬首以徇。

translations.literal: The troops then besieged the station, seized Guozhong, and beheaded him for public display.
translations.idiomatic: The troops surrounded the station, seized Guozhong, and beheaded him before the army.

sentences.zh: 是日，貴妃既縊，韓國、虢國二夫人亦為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: That day the Noble Consort was already strangled; the Ladies of Han and Guo states were also killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Noble Consort was strangled, and the Ladies of Han and Guo were killed by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫魏方進死，左相韋見素傷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin died; Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin was killed and Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu wounded.

sentences.zh: 良久兵解，陳玄禮等見上謝罪曰：「國忠撓敗國經，構興禍亂，使黎元塗炭，乘輿播越，此而不誅，患難未已。

translations.literal: After a long while the troops dispersed; Chen Xuanli and others came before the sovereign to apologize: "Guozhong thwarted and ruined the state norms, stirred up calamity and disorder, caused the black-haired people to be scorched in misery and the imperial carriage to flee in exile — if this man were not executed, disaster would not end.
translations.idiomatic: When the tumult subsided, Chen Xuanli and the others apologized to the emperor: "Guozhong wrecked the laws of the state and brought on disaster. The people burn and the throne is driven into exile. If he had not been killed, the calamity would never end.

sentences.zh: 臣等為社稷大計，請矯制之罪。」

translations.literal: We, for the great plan of altars and state, beg forgiveness for exercising authority under false imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: We acted for the realm and beg forgiveness for taking authority without your command.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕識之不明，任寄失所。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Our recognition was not clear; our appointments were misplaced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I failed to see clearly and chose the wrong men.

sentences.zh: 近亦覺悟，審其詐佞，意欲到蜀，肆諸市朝。

translations.literal: Recently we too have awakened, saw through his deceit and flattery, and intended upon reaching Shu to expose him in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: I have lately understood his deceit and meant, once we reached Shu, to expose him in the public square.

sentences.zh: 今神明啟卿，諧朕夙誌，將疇爵賞，何至言焉。」

translations.literal: now the spirits have enlightened you, harmonizing with our long-held purpose; we shall grant rank and reward — why speak thus of offense?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has moved you to fulfill my wish. I will grant you rank and reward. Why speak of guilt?"

sentences.zh: 是時，祿山雖據河洛，其兵鋒東止於梁、宋，南不過許、鄧。

translations.literal: At that time although Lushan held the He and Luo regions, his spearhead east stopped at Liang and Song, south it did not pass Xu and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lushan held the Yellow and Luo valleys, his advance east halted at Liang and Song and south at Xu and Deng.

sentences.zh: 李光弼、郭子儀統河朔勁卒，連收恆、定，若崤、函固守，兵不妄動，則AT逆之勢，不討自弊。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi commanded elite troops of Hebei, continuously recovered Heng and Ding; if Xiaomian and Hangu were firmly held and troops did not move rashly, then the rebel's momentum would collapse without being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi led Hebei's best troops and retook Heng and Ding. Had Xiaomian and Hangu been held and the army kept still, the rebels would have worn themselves out without a fight.

sentences.zh: 及哥舒翰出師，凡不數日，乘輿遷幸，朝廷陷沒，百僚系頸，妃主被戮，兵滿天下，毒流四海，皆國忠之召禍也。

translations.literal: When Geshu Han marched out, within but a few days the imperial carriage moved in exile, the court fell, a hundred officials bound by the neck, consorts and princesses slaughtered, troops filled the realm, poison spread across the four seas — all were disasters summoned by Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Geshu Han marched out, within days the emperor fled, the capital fell, officials were bound, princesses slain, and war and ruin spread across the realm — all calamities Guozhong brought upon himself.

sentences.zh: 國忠子：暄、昢、曉、晞。

translations.literal: Guozhong's sons: Xuan, Kuai, Xiao, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's sons were Xuan, Kuai, Xiao, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 暄為太常卿兼戶部侍郎，尚延和郡主；

translations.literal: Xuan was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, married to the Princess of Yanhe commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Minister of Revenue, married to the Princess of Yanhe;

sentences.zh: 昢為鴻臚卿，尚萬春公主。

translations.literal: Kuai was Chamberlain for Dependencies, married to the Princess of Wanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai was Chamberlain for Dependencies and married the Princess of Wanchun.

sentences.zh: 兄弟各立第於親仁裏，窮極奢侈。

translations.literal: The brothers each established mansions in Qinren ward, indulging to the utmost in luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Each brother built a mansion in Qinren Ward and lived in boundless luxury.

sentences.zh: 國忠娶蜀倡裴氏女曰裴柔，國忠既死，柔與虢國夫人皆自剄死。

translations.literal: Guozhong married the Shu courtesan surnamed Pei called Pei Rou; after Guozhong died, Rou and the Lady of Guo state both killed themselves by cutting the throat.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong had married the Shu singer Pei Rou. After his death she and the Lady of Guo killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 暄死於馬嵬；

translations.literal: Xuan died at Mawei;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died at Mawei;

sentences.zh: 昢陷賊被殺；

translations.literal: Kuai was trapped by rebels and killed;
translations.idiomatic: Kuai was caught by the rebels and killed;

sentences.zh: 曉走漢中郡，漢中王瑀榜殺之；

translations.literal: Xiao fled to Hanzhong commandery; Prince of Hanzhong Yu had him posted and killed;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao fled to Hanzhong, where Prince Yu had him hunted down and killed;

sentences.zh: 晞走至陳倉，為追兵所殺。

translations.literal: Xi fled to Chencang and was killed by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fled to Chencang and was killed by pursuers.

sentences.zh: 國忠之黨翰林學士張漸竇華、中書舍人宋昱、吏部郎中鄭昂等，憑國忠之勢，招來賂遺，車馬盈門，財貨山積；

translations.literal: Guozhong's partisans — Hanlin Academician Zhang Jian, Dou Hua, Secretariat Drafter Song Yu, Ministry of Personnel Section Chief Zheng Ang and others — relying on Guozhong's power, solicited bribes; carriages and horses filled their gates, wealth piled like mountains;
translations.idiomatic: His followers — the Hanlin scholar Zhang Jian, Dou Hua, the drafter Song Yu, the personnel director Zheng Ang, and others — traded on his power for bribes until their gates choked with carriages and their wealth rose like hills;

sentences.zh: 及國忠敗，皆坐誅滅，其斫喪王室，俱一時之沴氣焉。

translations.literal: when Guozhong fell they were all executed and exterminated; their destruction of the royal house was all one season's baleful vapor.
translations.idiomatic: when he fell they were all executed. Their ruin of the dynasty was the poison of a single age.

sentences.zh: 張暐，汝州襄城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei was a man of Xiangcheng in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei was from Xiangcheng in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖德政，武德中鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dezheng was Yanzhou prefect in the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dezheng had been prefect of Yanzhou under Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 暐，景龍初為銅鞮令，家本豪富，好賓客，以弋獵自娛。

translations.literal: Wei, at the start of the Jinglong era was magistrate of Tongdi; his family was originally wealthy; he loved guests and amused himself with archery and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jinglong era Wei was magistrate of Tongdi. His family was rich, he loved company, and he passed his days hunting.

sentences.zh: 會臨淄王為潞州別駕，暐潛識英姿，傾身事之，日奉遊處。

translations.literal: It happened that the King of Linzi was Vice-Prefect of Luzhou; Wei secretly recognized his heroic bearing and devoted himself to serving him, daily attending him in travel and pastimes.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Linzi served as vice-prefect of Luzhou, Wei saw his promise and gave himself wholly to the prince, sharing his days of sport and travel.

sentences.zh: 及樂人趙元禮自山東來，有女美麗，善歌舞，王幸之，止於暐第，生廢太子瑛。

translations.literal: When the musician Zhao Yuanli came from Shandong with a beautiful daughter skilled in song and dance, the king favored her and lodged at Wei's mansion; the deposed crown prince Ying was born.
translations.idiomatic: When the musician Zhao Yuanli came from the east with a beautiful daughter skilled in dance, the prince favored her and lodged her in Wei's house. There the future deposed Crown Prince Ying was born.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年六月，王清內難，升為皇太子，召暐拜宮門大夫，每與諸王、姜皎、崔滌、李令問、王守一、薛伯陽在太子左右以接歡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tanglong, when the king cleared internal turmoil and was elevated to crown prince, Wei was summoned and appointed Palace Gate Grandee; he was constantly with the various princes, Jiang Jiao, Cui Ti, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, and Xue Boyang at the prince's side to share pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tanglong, when the prince quelled the palace turmoil and became heir, he summoned Wei as Palace Gate Grandee. Wei joined the princes, Jiang Jiao, Cui Ti, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, and Xue Boyang in the heir's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 其年，擢拜左臺侍御史，數月遷左御史臺中丞。

translations.literal: That year he was promoted to Left Platform Attending Censor; within months he was transferred to Left Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made attending censor of the Left Platform and within months vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，太子即位，帝居武德殿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian the crown prince ascended the throne; the emperor resided at Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian the crown prince took the throne while the retired emperor remained at Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 太平公主有異謀，廣樹朋黨，暐與僕射劉幽求請先為備。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping harbored a separate plot and widely planted factions; Wei together with Vice Director Liu Youqiu asked to prepare first.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping plotted treason and built a wide faction. Wei and the chief minister Liu Youqiu urged the emperor to prepare.

sentences.zh: 太平聞之，白於睿宗，乃流暐於嶺南峰州，幽求謫於嶺外。

translations.literal: Taiping heard of it and reported to Ruizong; Wei was then exiled to Fengzhou in Lingnan, Youqiu demoted beyond the ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping learned of it and told Ruizong. Wei was exiled to Fengzhou in the far south and Youqiu banished beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 及太平之敗，幽求追拜尚書左僕射、兼侍中；

translations.literal: When Taiping was defeated, Youqiu was recalled and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping fell, Youqiu was recalled as left vice director of the Secretariat and palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 暐為大理卿，封鄧國公，實封三百戶，逾月又加權兼雍州長史。

translations.literal: Wei became Minister of Justice, enfeoffed Duke of Deng state with substantive fief of three hundred households; after a month he was additionally granted acting Metropolitan Prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei became minister of justice, was enfeoffed as Duke of Deng with three hundred households, and a month later was made acting prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，改元開元，以雍州為京兆府，長史為尹。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year the era name changed to Kaiyuan; Yongzhou was made the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture, and the prefect was styled yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year the era became Kaiyuan, Yongzhou was renamed Jingzhao Prefecture, and its prefect was titled yin.

sentences.zh: 暐首遷京兆尹，入侍宴私，出主都政，以為榮寵之極。

translations.literal: Wei was first transferred to Jingzhao yin; attending banquets in private within, overseeing capital administration without — regarded as the utmost in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was the first to hold the post of Jingzhao yin — feasting with the emperor within the palace, governing the capital without. Men called it the summit of favor.

sentences.zh: 暐亦有應務才幹，遷太子詹事，判尚書左右丞，再除左羽林大將軍，三為左金吾大將軍，又為殿中監、太仆卿。

translations.literal: Wei also had talent for practical affairs; he was transferred to Crown Prince Steward, concurrently judged the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Secretariat, twice appointed Left Forest Martial General, thrice Left Golden Host General, and also Director of the Palace Directorate and Grand Stablemaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was capable in office as well. He became crown prince steward, served concurrently as vice director of the Secretariat, twice commanded the Left Forest Army, thrice the Left Golden Host, and also directed the palace workshops and the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以暐年高，加特進。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, because Wei was advanced in age, he was specially granted tejin.
translations.idiomatic: In his twentieth year of service he was granted the honorary rank of tejin for his great age.

sentences.zh: 子履冰、季良、弟晤皆居清列。

translations.literal: His sons Lvbing and Jiliang and younger brother Wu all held pure, elevated posts.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lvbing and Jiliang and his brother Wu all held high, honorable offices.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，暐還鄉拜掃，特賜錦袍繒彩，禦賜詩以寵異之，乘傳來往，敕郡縣供擬。

translations.literal: At the start of the Tianbao era Wei returned home for tomb-sweeping; he was specially granted brocade robes and silks, the emperor composing a verse to show special favor; he traveled by relay post back and forth, with edicts for commanderies and counties to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he returned home to sweep the tombs. The emperor gave him brocade robes and silks and composed a poem in his honor. He traveled by imperial relay and every county was ordered to supply him.

sentences.zh: 暐鬢髮華皓，在輿中，子弟車馬連接數里，衣冠榮之。

translations.literal: Wei's temples and hair were hoary white; in the carriage his sons and younger kinsmen's horses and carriages linked for several li; the gentry honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's hair was snow-white in his carriage while sons and kin stretched in a line of horses for miles. The gentry looked on with envy.

sentences.zh: 中使中路追賜藥物。

translations.literal: Palace envoys on the road pursued and bestowed medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys overtook him on the road with imperial medicines.

sentences.zh: 至襄城月餘，詔還京。

translations.literal: After more than a month at Xiangcheng, an edict ordered return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a month at Xiangcheng he was ordered back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五載薨，年九十餘，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; over ninety years of age; posthumously granted Grand Master for the Palace with honorary rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, past ninety, and was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with the rank of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 其後，履冰為金吾將軍，季良殿中監，俱列啟戟，時人美之。

translations.literal: Thereafter Lvbing was Golden Host general, Jiliang Director of the Palace Directorate; both listed among those bearing halberds at audience — men of the time praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lvbing became a Golden Host general and Jiliang director of the palace workshops; both bore halberds at court, and men praised the family.

sentences.zh: 暐壽考。

translations.literal: Wei lived to great old age.
translations.idiomatic: Wei lived to great old age.

sentences.zh: 善保終始。

translations.literal: He knew well how to preserve himself from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to keep fortune from first to last.

sentences.zh: 王琚，懷州河內人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ju was a man of Henei in Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju was from Henei in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 叔父隱客，則天朝為鳳閣侍郎。

translations.literal: His uncle's son Yinke was Vice-Director of the Phoenix Pavilion in the Zetian court.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yinke had been vice-director of the Phoenix Pavilion under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 琚少孤而聰敏，有才略，好玄象合煉之學。

translations.literal: Ju was orphaned young yet clever and keen, with talent and stratagem, fond of dark-learning astrology and elixir-smelting arts.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Ju was clever and resourceful, drawn to astrology and the alchemist's arts.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，年二十餘，嘗謁駙馬王同皎，同皎甚器之，益歡洽。

translations.literal: At the start of the Shendragon era, aged a little over twenty, he once visited Chief Commandant Wang Tongjiao; Tongjiao greatly esteemed him and their intimacy deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shendragon era, in his twenties, he visited the imperial son-in-law Wang Tongjiao, who took a great liking to him and drew him close.

sentences.zh: 言及刺武三思事，琚義而許之，與周璟、張仲之為忘年之友。

translations.literal: Speaking of assassinating Wu Sansi, Ju took it as righteous and promised; with Zhou Jing and Zhang Zhongzhi he became friends despite difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: When they spoke of killing Wu Sansi, Ju pledged himself on principle and became a sworn friend of Zhou Jing and Zhang Zhongzhi, though they were older.

sentences.zh: 及同皎敗，琚恐為吏所捕，變姓名詣於江都，傭書於富商家，主人後悟其非傭者，以女嫁之，資給其財。

translations.literal: When Tongjiao was defeated Ju feared capture by officials, changed his name and went to Jiangdu, hired out as scribe to a wealthy merchant; the master later realized he was no mere hireling, married his daughter to him and supplied him with wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongjiao fell, Ju fled under a false name to Jiangdu and copied books for a rich merchant. The man saw he was no common clerk, gave him his daughter, and set him up with money.

sentences.zh: 經四五年，睿宗登極，琚具白主人，厚資其行裝，乃至長安。

translations.literal: After four or five years Ruizong ascended the throne; Ju fully told his master, who richly supplied his travel gear, and he reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Four or five years later Ruizong took the throne. Ju told his host everything; the man gave him a rich outfit for the road, and Ju reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 遇玄宗為太子監國，為太平公主所忌，思立孱弱，以竊威權，太子憂危。

translations.literal: He encountered Xuanzong as regent crown prince, ostracized by Princess Taiping; she thought to establish a weakling to seize power; the crown prince was in peril.
translations.idiomatic: He found Xuanzong serving as regent while the crown prince, hated by Princess Taiping, who meant to set up a weak ruler and seize power, lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 沙門普潤先與玄宗筮，克清內難，加三品，食實封，常入太子宮。

translations.literal: The monk Puyun had earlier divined for Xuanzong that internal trouble would be overcome; he was raised three ranks with substantive fief, and often entered the crown prince's palace.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Puyun had divined victory over the palace foes for Xuanzong, was raised three ranks with a substantive fief, and often came to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 琚見之，說以天時人事，歷然可觀。

translations.literal: Ju met him and discoursed on celestial timing and human affairs as plainly observable.
translations.idiomatic: Ju met him and spoke of heaven's signs and men's affairs as clear as daylight.

sentences.zh: 普潤白玄宗，玄宗異之。

translations.literal: Puyun reported to Xuanzong; Xuanzong was struck with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Puyun told Xuanzong, and the prince marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 及琚於吏部選補諸暨主簿，於東宮過謝，及殿，而行徐視高，中官曰：「殿下在簾下。」

translations.literal: When Ju was at the Ministry of Personnel selecting and filling the post of Zhuji county chief clerk, he passed the Eastern Palace to pay respects; upon reaching the hall he walked slowly, gaze lifted high; the palace attendant said: "The heir apparent is behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju was appointed chief clerk of Zhuji through the Ministry of Personnel, he called at the Eastern Palace to give thanks. He entered the hall walking slowly with his eyes raised. A eunuch said, "His Highness is behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「在外只聞有太平公主，不聞有太子。

translations.literal: Ju said: "Outside one hears only of Princess Taiping, not of a crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "Outside these walls one hears only of Princess Taiping, not of a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子有大功於社稷，大孝於君親，何得有此聲？」

translations.literal: The crown prince has great merit toward the altars and great filial piety toward lord and parent — how can there be such a reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has saved the realm and shown supreme filial piety. How can his name be so dim?"

sentences.zh: 玄宗遽召見之，琚曰：「頃韋庶人智識淺短，親行弒逆，人心盡搖，思立李氏，殿下誅之為易。

translations.literal: Xuanzong hastily summoned him; Ju said: "Recently Empress Wei had shallow understanding and personally carried out regicide; people's hearts were all shaken, yearning to establish the Li; the heir apparent could have executed her with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong summoned him at once. Ju said, "When Empress Wei murdered the emperor, the realm yearned for the House of Li. You could have destroyed her with ease.

sentences.zh: 今社稷已安，太平則天之女，兇狡無比，專思立功，朝之大臣，多為其用。

translations.literal: Now the altars are already secure; Taiping is Wu Zetian's daughter, incomparably fierce and crafty, intent only on establishing merit; many court great ministers are used by her.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is settled now, but Taiping is Wu Zetian's daughter — fierce beyond measure, hungry for power — and most of the great ministers serve her.

sentences.zh: 主上以元妹之愛，能忍其過。

translations.literal: The lord emperor from love of a younger sister by the same mother can bear her faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loves her as his younger sister and forgives her faults.

sentences.zh: 賤臣淺識，為殿下深憂。」

translations.literal: This mean servant's shallow understanding is deeply worried on the heir apparent's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: I am only a humble man, but I am deeply afraid for Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 玄宗命之同榻而坐。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered him to sit on the same couch.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had him sit on the same couch.

sentences.zh: 玄宗泣曰：「四哥仁孝，同氣唯有太平，言之恐有違犯，不言憂患轉深，為臣為子，計無所出。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong wept and said: "Fourth Brother is benevolent and filial; among those of the same breath there is only Taiping; to speak of her I fear violation, not to speak the peril grows deeper — as minister and as son I have no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong wept and said, "My brother the emperor is kind and filial. Of our blood there is only Taiping left. To speak against her is treason; to stay silent is worse. As son and subject I see no way.

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「天子之孝，貴於安宗廟。

translations.literal: Ju said: "The son of heaven's filial piety lies in securing the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "A son of heaven's true filial piety is to secure the ancestral temples

sentences.zh: 定萬人。

translations.literal: and in stabilizing the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: and to give peace to the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 征之於昔，蓋主，漢帝之長姊，帝幼，蓋主共養帝於宮中，後與上官桀、燕王謀害大司馬霍光，不議及君上，漢主恐危劉氏，以大義去之。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity — Princess Gaoyang was the Han emperor's elder sister; when the emperor was young Gaoyang together raised him in the palace; later with Shangguan Jie and the Prince of Yan she plotted to harm Grand Marshal Huo Guang, not debating whether to touch the sovereign — the Han lord feared danger to the Liu clan and removed her by great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Look to the past. Princess Gaoyang was the Han emperor's elder sister and raised him in the palace. Later she joined Shangguan Jie and the Prince of Yan against Huo Guang. The emperor, fearing for the Liu clan, cast her off for the sake of the realm.

sentences.zh: 況殿下功格天地，位尊儲貳。

translations.literal: How much more so — your merit spans heaven and earth, your position honored as heir!
translations.idiomatic: Your merit fills heaven and earth, and you stand as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太平雖姑，臣妾也，何敢議之！

translations.literal: Taiping though an aunt is yet a subject — how dare one debate her!
translations.idiomatic: Taiping is your aunt, but she is still a subject. Who would hesitate to judge her?

sentences.zh: 今劉幽求、張說、郭元振一二大臣，心輔殿下。

translations.literal: Now Liu Youqiu, Zhang Yue, Guo Yuanzhen and one or two great ministers loyally assist the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu, Zhang Yue, Guo Yuanzhen, and other great ministers stand loyal to you.

sentences.zh: 太平之黨，必有移奪安危之計，不可立談。」

translations.literal: Taiping's faction will certainly have plots to shift and seize safety and peril — this cannot be discussed in the open."
translations.idiomatic: Her faction will surely move to seize power. This is not a matter to speak of openly."

sentences.zh: 玄宗又曰：「公有何小藝，可隱跡與寡人遊處？」

translations.literal: Xuanzong also said: "Sir, what small arts do you have whereby you might hide your traces and wander with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong asked again, "What humble skills do you have, that you might keep close to me in secret?"

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「飛丹煉藥，談諧嘲詠，堪與優人比肩。」

translations.literal: Ju said: "Flying cinnabar and refining medicine, banter and mocking verse — fit to stand shoulder to shoulder with actors."
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "Refining elixirs, jesting, and composing doggerel — skills fit to rank with the palace players."

sentences.zh: 玄宗益喜，與之為友，恨相知晚，呼為王十一。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was increasingly pleased, befriended him, regretted meeting late, and called him Eleventh Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong grew still more delighted, took him as a friend, lamented that they had met so late, and nicknamed him "Wang Eleven."

sentences.zh: 翌日，奏授詹事府司直、內供奉兼崇文學士，日與諸王及姜皎等侍奉焉，獨琚常預秘計。

translations.literal: The next day, a memorial appointed him Registrar of the Heir Apparent's Household, inner attendant and concurrent Scholar of the Chongwen Academy; daily he attended with the princes and Jiang Jiao and others; only Ju constantly joined secret plans.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was appointed registrar in the Heir Apparent's household, inner attendant, and scholar of the Chongwen Academy. Day after day he waited on the princes and Jiang Jiao and the rest, while Ju alone was regularly let in on confidential designs.

sentences.zh: 逾月，又拜太子舍人，尋又兼諫議大夫、內供奉，又贈其父故下邽丞仲友楚州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he was again appointed Crown Prince Attendant; soon also concurrent Censor and inner attendant; also posthumously granted his father, the former assistant of Xiaji County Zhongyou, as Governor of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made crown prince attendant, then censor and inner attendant as well. His father Zhongyou, formerly assistant magistrate of Xiaji, was posthumously honored as governor of Chu.

sentences.zh: 先天元年七月，玄宗居尊位，在武德殿。

translations.literal: First year of Xiantian, seventh month, Xuanzong occupied the seat of honor at Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xiantian, Xuanzong took the throne at Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 八月，擢拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Eighth month, promoted and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時劉幽求、張暐並流於嶺外，琚見事迫，請早為之計。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Youqiu and Zhang Wei were both exiled beyond the Ling range; Ju saw affairs pressing and asked to plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu and Zhang Wei had both been banished south of the Ling Mountains. Seeing events closing in, Ju urged that they act while there was still time.

sentences.zh: 二年七月三日，琚與岐王範、薛王業、姜皎、李令問、王毛仲、王守一並預誅逆，以鐵騎至承天門。

translations.literal: Second year, seventh month, third day, Ju with the Prince of Qi Fan, Prince of Xue Ye, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi all took part in executing the rebels, with iron cavalry reaching Chengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the seventh month in the second year, Ju joined the Princes of Qi and Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi in putting down the traitors and rode armored cavalry to Chengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗聞鼓噪聲，召郭元振升承天樓，宣詔下關，侍御史任知古召募數百人於朝堂，不得入。

translations.literal: At that time Ruizong heard the clamor of drums, summoned Guo Yuanzhen up Chengtian Tower, proclaimed an edict down the pass; Supervising Censor Ren Zhigu recruited several hundred men in the court hall but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong heard the uproar and summoned Guo Yuanzhen to Chengtian Tower to proclaim an edict down the gate. Supervising censor Ren Zhigu mustered several hundred men in the court hall but could not get through.

sentences.zh: 頃間，琚等從玄宗至樓上，誅蕭至忠、岑義、竇懷貞、常元楷、李慈、李猷等。

translations.literal: Shortly, Ju and others followed Xuanzong to the tower top and executed Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, Dou Huaihen, Chang Yuankai, Li Ci, Li You, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ju and the others followed Xuanzong to the upper tower and put to death Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, Dou Huaihen, Chang Yuankai, Li Ci, Li You, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 睿宗遜居百福殿。

translations.literal: Ruizong yielded residence to Baifu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong withdrew to Baifu Hall.

sentences.zh: 十日，拜琚銀青光祿大夫、戶部尚書，封趙國公，食實封五百戶；

translations.literal: Tenth day, appointed Ju Silver-Green Spark Grand Master of Splendid Honor and Minister of Revenue, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, substantive fief five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day Ju was made silver-green grand master of splendid honor and minister of revenue, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with a substantive fief of five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 皎銀青光祿大夫、工部尚書，封楚國公，實封五百戶；

translations.literal: Jiao Silver-Green Spark Grand Master of Splendid Honor and Minister of Works, enfeoffed Duke of Chu, substantive fief five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiao received the same grand master rank and the ministry of works, was made Duke of Chu with five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 令問銀青光祿大夫、殿中監、宋國公，實封三百戶；

translations.literal: Lingwen Silver-Green Spark Grand Master of Splendid Honor, Director of the Palace Directorate, Duke of Song, substantive fief three hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingwen became grand master, director of the palace directorate, and Duke of Song with three hundred households;

sentences.zh: 毛仲輔國大將軍、左武衛大將軍、檢校閑廄兼知監牧使、霍國公，實封五百戶；

translations.literal: Maozhong Assistant State General, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, commissioner inspecting the outer stud farms and also supervising pastures, Duke of Huo, substantive fief five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhong was made assistant state general and grand general of the left martial guard, with charge of the outer stud farms and pasture administration, Duke of Huo with five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 守一銀青光祿大夫、太常卿員外置同正員，進封晉國公，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Shouyi Silver-Green Spark Grand Master of Splendid Honor, Vice Minister of Rites on extra roster with same regular rank, advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Jin, substantive fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouyi received the grand master rank, was named vice minister of rites on an extra roster with full ministerial standing, and was advanced to Duke of Jin with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 琚、皎、令問並固讓尚書、殿中監，不上。

translations.literal: Ju, Jiao, and Lingwen all firmly declined the ministries and the palace directorship and did not assume them.
translations.idiomatic: Ju, Jiao, and Lingwen all firmly declined the ministerial posts and the palace directorship and never took them up.

sentences.zh: 十八日，琚、皎依舊官各加實封二百戶，通前七百戶。

translations.literal: Eighteenth day, Ju and Jiao per their original posts each received an additional substantive fief of two hundred households, seven hundred in all with prior.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day Ju and Jiao, retaining their former titles, were each granted two hundred more households in substantive fief, seven hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 累日，玄宗宴於內殿，賜功臣金銀器皿各一床、雜彩各一千匹、絹一千匹，列於庭，宴慰終夕，載之而歸。

translations.literal: Over several days Xuanzong feasted in the inner hall, bestowing on the meritorious officials gold and silver vessels each one couch-load, assorted silks each one thousand bolts, silk each one thousand bolts, arrayed in the courtyard; feasted and comforted until night's end, loaded them and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: For days on end Xuanzong feasted them in the inner hall and gave each meritorious official a couch-load of gold and silver vessels, a thousand bolts of patterned silks, and a thousand bolts of plain silk, all set out in the courtyard. The revel lasted the whole night, and they drove home laden with gifts.

sentences.zh: 琚轉見恩顧，每延入閣中，迄夜方出。

translations.literal: Ju increasingly saw favor; each time he was summoned into the inner quarters and did not leave until night.
translations.idiomatic: Ju grew ever more favored. He was summoned into the inner quarters night after night and did not emerge until dawn.

sentences.zh: 歸休之日，中官至第召之。

translations.literal: On his days of rest, eunuchs came to his residence to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Even on his days off, eunuchs came to his house to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 中官亦使尚宮就琚宅問訊琚母，時果珍味賫之，助其甘旨。

translations.literal: Eunuchs also sent palace women to Ju's house to inquire after Ju's mother, sending seasonal fruits and delicacies to aid their savory fare.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs also sent palace women to Ju's home to inquire after his mother, bearing seasonal fruit and delicacies for her table.

sentences.zh: 琚在帷幄之側，常參聞大政，時人謂之「內宰相」，無有比者。

translations.literal: Ju beside the curtains constantly heard great policies; people of the time called him the 'inner chancellor,' without equal.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's side Ju was privy to weighty affairs of state. Men of the day called him the "inner chancellor," and none could rival him.

sentences.zh: 又贈其父魏州刺史。

translations.literal: Also posthumously granted his father as Governor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father was again posthumously honored as governor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 或有上說於玄宗曰：「彼王琚、麻嗣宗譎詭縱橫之士，可與履危，不可得誌。

translations.literal: Some submitted to Xuanzong saying: 'Those Wang Ju and Ma Sizong are crafty men of devious stratagems; with them one may tread danger, one cannot bring them to achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Xuanzong, saying, "Wang Ju and Ma Sizong are devious schemers. They are fit for perilous times, not for bringing a realm to fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 天下已定，宜益求純樸經術之士。」

translations.literal: The realm is already settled; one should increasingly seek men of pure simplicity and classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is settled now. Your Majesty should look instead for men of plain integrity trained in the classics.

sentences.zh: 玄宗乃疏之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong then kept them at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong thereupon kept them at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 十一月，令御史大夫持節巡天兵以北諸軍。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, ordered the Grand Censor to bear the staff and tour the armies north of Tianbing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he ordered the grand censor, bearing imperial credentials, to inspect the armies north of Tianbing.

sentences.zh: 十二月，改年號為開元，又改官名，與蘇颋同為紫微侍郎。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, changed the era name to Kaiyuan, also changed official titles; with Su Ting together as Vice Directors of Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the era name was changed to Kaiyuan and official titles were revised. Ju and Su Ting served together as vice directors of the Ziwei Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年二月回，未及京，便除澤州刺史，削封。

translations.literal: Second year, second month he returned; before reaching the capital he was removed as Governor of Ze and his enfeoffment was cut.
translations.idiomatic: He returned in the second month of the second year, but before he reached the capital he was appointed governor of Ze and stripped of his noble rank.

sentences.zh: 歷衡、郴、滑、虢、沔、夔、許、潤九州刺史，又復其封。

translations.literal: He passed through nine prefectures as governor—Heng, Chen, Hua, Guo, Mian, Kui, Xu, and Run—and again had his enfeoffment restored.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Heng, Chen, Hua, Guo, Mian, Kui, Xu, and Run, and his noble title was eventually restored.

sentences.zh: 二十年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, he mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，起復右庶子，兼巂州刺史，又改同、蒲、通、鄧、蔡五州刺史。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, recalled from mourning as Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household and also Governor of Su; again changed through the five prefectures of Tong, Pu, Tong, Deng, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was recalled from mourning as right vice director of the heir apparent's household and governor of Su, then served in turn at Tong, Pu, Tong, Deng, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 天寶後，又為廣平、鄴郡二太守。

translations.literal: After Tianbao, he again served as prefect of Guangping and Ye commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era he was again prefect of Guangping and of Ye.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，著勛中朝，又食實封，典十五州，常受饋遺，下檐帳設，皆數千貫。

translations.literal: By nature extravagant; held merit at court, also received substantive fief, administered fifteen prefectures, constantly received gifts; lower-hall tents and furnishings all ran to several thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was lavish. He had earned merit at court, drew a substantive fief, and governed fifteen prefectures. Gifts poured in constantly, and the tents and furnishings of his lower halls each cost thousands of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 玄宗念舊，常優容之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong remembering old ties constantly indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering old ties, Xuanzong indulged him.

sentences.zh: 侍兒二十人，皆居寶帳。

translations.literal: Twenty serving girls, all dwelt in precious tents.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty serving women lived in jeweled pavilions.

sentences.zh: 家累三百餘口，作造不遵於法式。

translations.literal: His household exceeded three hundred mouths; building and manufacture did not follow regulations.
translations.idiomatic: His household numbered more than three hundred souls, and his building projects ignored the regulations.

sentences.zh: 雖居州伯，與佐官、胥吏、酋豪連榻飲謔，或樗蒱、藏钅句以為樂。

translations.literal: Though occupying a prefect's seat, with aides, clerks, and local chiefs he shared couches drinking and jesting, or played pitch-pot and hoarded gaming stakes for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held a prefect's rank, he shared couches with aides, clerks, and local magnates, drinking and joking, or amused himself with pitch-pot and games of chance.

sentences.zh: 每移一州，車馬填路，數里不絕。

translations.literal: Each transfer to a new prefecture, carriages and horses filled the road for several li without break.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he moved to a new prefecture, his train of carriages and horses filled the road for miles.

sentences.zh: 攜妓從禽，恣為歡賞，垂四十年矣。

translations.literal: Leading courtesans and following the hunt, he indulged in pleasure, nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: He took courtesans on the hunt and gave himself over to pleasure for nearly forty years.

sentences.zh: 時李邕、王弼與琚皆年齒尊高，久在外郡，書疏尺題來往，有「譴謫留落」之句。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yong, Wang Bi, and Ju were all advanced in years, long in outer prefectures; letters and notes passed between them with phrases of 'banished and stranded.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, Wang Bi, and Ju were all elderly by then and had long served in distant prefectures. In their letters they exchanged phrases about exile and being left behind.

sentences.zh: 右相林甫以琚等負材使氣，陰議除之。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Li Linfu, because Ju and others possessed talent and were proud in spirit, secretly plotted to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Li Linfu, finding Ju and the others talented but overbearing, secretly plotted to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 五載正月，琚果為林甫構成其罪，貶琚江華郡員外司馬，削階封。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, Ju indeed had crimes fabricated by Linfu; demoted Ju to External Acting Administrator of Jianghua commandery and cut ranks and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Linfu duly framed charges against Ju, who was demoted to acting administrator of Jianghua and stripped of rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 至任未幾，林甫使羅希奭重按之。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching his post, Linfu sent Luo Xizhi to reinvestigate heavily.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken up his post when Linfu sent Luo Xizhi to reopen the case.

sentences.zh: 希奭排馬牒至，琚懼，仰藥，竟不能死；

translations.literal: Xizhi dispatched a warrant by post horse; Ju feared, took poison by mouth, yet could not die;
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi's warrant arrived by relay horse. In terror Ju swallowed poison, but it did not kill him;

sentences.zh: 及希奭至，遂自縊而卒。

translations.literal: When Xizhi arrived, he then hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: when Xizhi arrived, he hanged himself and died.

sentences.zh: 死非其罪，人用憐之。

translations.literal: Death not for his crimes; people pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: He had not deserved death, and the world pitied him.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: First year of Baoying, posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying he was posthumously made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 王毛仲，本高麗人也。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhong was originally a man of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhong was a native of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 父遊擊將軍職事求婁，犯事沒官，生毛仲，因隸於玄宗。

translations.literal: His father Youji, a general of the strike corps on duty in Qiulou, committed an offense and was confiscated as an official; he bore Maozhong, who thus came under Xuanzong's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Youji, a strike-corps officer serving in Qiulou, was convicted and enslaved to the state. Maozhong was born in bondage and thus entered Xuanzong's household.

sentences.zh: 性識明悟，玄宗為臨淄王，常伏事左右。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent and perceptive; when Xuanzong was Prince of Linzi, he constantly attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted by nature, he waited on Xuanzong constantly when the latter was Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 及出兼潞州別駕，又見李宜德趫捷善騎射，為人蒼頭，以錢五萬買之。

translations.literal: When he went out also serving as Vice Prefect of Lu, he again met Li Yide, nimble and skilled at mounted archery, serving as a groom; he bought him for fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong went out to serve concurrently as vice prefect of Lu, he noticed Li Yide, a swift groom skilled in horsemanship and archery, and bought him for fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年冬，玄宗還長安，以二人挾弓矢為翼。

translations.literal: Winter of the third year of Jinglong, Xuanzong returned to Chang'an, with the two men carrying bows as wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Jinglong, when Xuanzong returned to Chang'an, the two men bore bows at his side like wings.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗貞觀中，擇官戶蕃口中少年驍勇者百人，每出遊獵，令持弓矢於禦馬前射生，令騎豹文韉，著畫獸文衫，謂之「百騎」。

translations.literal: Initially, in Zhenguan of Taizong, from official households and tribal youth he selected a hundred valiant young men; each time going out to hunt he ordered them to hold bows before the imperial horses to shoot game, ride leopard-pattern girths, wear painted beast shirts, called the 'Hundred Riders.'
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong in the Zhenguan era, a hundred bold youths were chosen from official households and tribal levies. On the hunt they rode before the imperial horses with bows to bring down game, wore leopard-pattern saddles and painted beast tunics, and were called the Hundred Riders.

sentences.zh: 至則天時，漸加其人，謂之「千騎」，分隸左右羽林營。

translations.literal: By Empress Wu's time the men were gradually increased; they were called the 'Thousand Riders' and assigned to the left and right Feathered Forest camps.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu their numbers grew until they were called the Thousand Riders and were divided between the left and right Feathered Forest camps.

sentences.zh: 孝和謂之「萬騎」，亦置使以領之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiahe called them the 'Ten Thousand Riders' and also placed commissioners to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhong renamed them the Ten Thousand Riders and appointed commissioners to command them.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在籓邸時，常接其豪俊者，或賜飲食財帛，以此盡歸心焉。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was at his princely residence he often received their bold stalwarts, sometimes bestowing food, drink, and wealth, thereby winning all their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was still at his princely residence he cultivated their boldest men, sometimes bestowing food, drink, and money, and so won their complete loyalty.

sentences.zh: 毛仲亦悟玄宗旨，待之甚謹，玄宗益憐其敏惠。

translations.literal: Maozhong also grasped Xuanzong's intent, served very diligently, and Xuanzong increasingly favored his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong too divined what Xuanzong wanted and served him scrupulously, and the prince grew fonder of his quick mind.

sentences.zh: 及四年六月，中宗遇弒，韋後稱制，令韋播、高嵩為羽林將軍，令押千騎營，榜棰以取威。

translations.literal: By the sixth month of the fourth year Zhongzong met assassination; Empress Wei assumed regency, appointed Wei Bo and Gao Song as Feathered Forest generals, ordered them to command the Thousand Riders camp, wielding cudgels to take authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year Zhongzong was murdered. Empress Wei seized power, made Wei Bo and Gao Song generals of the Feathered Forest, and put them over the Thousand Riders camp, using the lash to enforce their will.

sentences.zh: 其營長葛福順、陳玄禮等相與見玄宗訴冤，會玄宗已與劉幽求、麻嗣宗、薛崇簡等謀舉大計，相顧益歡，令幽求諷之，皆願決死從命。

translations.literal: Their camp chiefs Ge Fushun, Chen Xuanli, and others together went to see Xuanzong to plead injustice; it happened Xuanzong had already with Liu Youqiu, Ma Sizong, Xue Chongjian, and others plotted the great design; looking at one another they grew more joyful; he ordered Youqiu to sound them out; all vowed to follow unto death.
translations.idiomatic: The camp chiefs Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli came together to Xuanzong to plead their grievance. He had already been plotting with Liu Youqiu, Ma Sizong, and Xue Chongjian. Their eyes met in growing elation. Youqiu sounded the men out, and all swore to follow him to the death.

sentences.zh: 及二十日夜，玄宗入宛中，宜德從焉，毛仲避之不入。

translations.literal: On the night of the twentieth Xuanzong entered the park; Yide followed; Maozhong avoided it and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twentieth Xuanzong entered the imperial park. Yide went with him, but Maozhong held back and did not go in.

sentences.zh: 乙夜，福順等至，玄宗曰：「與公等除大逆，安社稷，各取富貴，在於俄頃，何以取信？」

translations.literal: Second watch, Fushun and others arrived; Xuanzong said: 'With you gentlemen we eliminate great traitors and secure the altars of soil and grain; each may take wealth and honor in a moment—how shall you be believed?
translations.idiomatic: In the second watch Fushun and the others arrived. Xuanzong said, "With you I will destroy these great traitors and secure the realm. Wealth and rank are yours in an instant. How can I convince you?

sentences.zh: 福順等請號而行，斯須斬韋播、韋璿、高嵩等頭來，玄宗舉火視之。

translations.literal: Fushun and others asked to advance under battle cry; in an instant severed heads of Wei Bo, Wei Jun, Gao Song, and others were brought; Xuanzong raised a torch to view them.
translations.idiomatic: They asked leave to charge under the battle cry. Moments later the heads of Wei Bo, Wei Jun, Gao Song, and the rest were brought in. Xuanzong held up a torch to look at them.

sentences.zh: 又召鐘紹京領總監丁匠刀鋸百人至，因斬關而入，後及安樂公主等皆為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Again summoned Zhong Shaojing leading a hundred master craftsmen with saws from the Directorate; thereby cut through the gate and entered; later the Empress and Princess Anle and others were all killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Zhong Shaojing with a hundred craftsmen bearing saws from the imperial workshops. They cut through the gate and poured in. The empress, Princess Anle, and the others were all slain by the mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 其夜，少帝以玄宗著大勛，進封平王。

translations.literal: That night, because Xuanzong had great merit, the Young Emperor advanced him to Prince of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: That same night the young emperor, honoring Xuanzong's great merit, advanced him to Prince of Ping.

sentences.zh: 以紹京、幽求知政事，署詔敕。

translations.literal: Appointed Shaojing and Youqiu to know government affairs and draft edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing and Youqiu were put in charge of state affairs and ordered to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 崇簡、嗣宗及福順、宜德，功大者為將軍，次者為中郎將。

translations.literal: Chongjian, Sizong, and Fushun and Yide—the greatest merit made generals, the next rank made palace guard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian, Sizong, Fushun, and Yide were rewarded according to merit: the greatest became generals, the rest commanders of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 其時，梓宮在殯，舉城縞素。

translations.literal: At that time the coffined emperor lay in state; the whole city was in white mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor still lay in state, and the whole city wore mourning white.

sentences.zh: 及明，玄宗引新立功者皆衣紫衣緋，持滿鐵騎而出，傾城聚觀歡慰。

translations.literal: At dawn Xuanzong led those newly achieving merit, all wearing purple coats and scarlet, holding fully strung iron cavalry forth; the whole city gathered to watch, rejoicing and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xuanzong led out his newly honored men in purple coats and scarlet, armored cavalry with bows strung. The whole city poured out to watch and rejoice.

sentences.zh: 其犯逆者，盡曝屍於城外。

translations.literal: The rebel criminals were all exposed as corpses outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The bodies of the traitors were displayed outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 毛仲數日而歸，玄宗不責，又超授將軍。

translations.literal: Maozhong returned after several days; Xuanzong did not blame him and again leap-promoted him to general.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong returned after several days. Xuanzong did not reproach him and promoted him straight to general.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗為皇太子監國，因奏改左右萬騎左右營為龍武軍，與左右羽林為北門四軍，以福順等為將軍以押之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong as Crown Prince supervised the state, he memorialized to change the left and right Ten Thousand Riders' left and right camps into the Dragon Martial Army, with the left and right Feathered Forest as the four northern gate armies, appointing Fushun and others as generals to command them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong became crown prince regent, he memorialized to rename the left and right Ten Thousand Rider camps the Dragon Martial Army and, together with the left and right Feathered Forest, to form the four northern gate armies, with Fushun and the others as their generals.

sentences.zh: 龍武官盡功臣，受錫賫，號為「唐元功臣」。

translations.literal: Dragon Martial officers were all meritorious subjects, received bestowals, and were styled 'meritorious subjects at the founding of Tang.'
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Martial corps was made up entirely of meritorious men who received imperial gifts and were styled "founders of the Tang restoration."

sentences.zh: 長安良家子避征徭，納資以求隸於其中，遂每軍至數千人。

translations.literal: Sons of good Chang'an families avoided corvee labor, paid funds to seek enrollment among them, and thus each army reached several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Well-born youths of Chang'an paid to join the corps and escape corvee duty, and each army soon numbered several thousand.

sentences.zh: 毛仲專知東宮駝馬鷹狗等坊，未逾年，已至大將軍，階三品矣。

translations.literal: Maozhong solely managed the Eastern Palace camel, horse, hawk, and dog yards; within less than a year he had already reached Grand General, third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong was put in sole charge of the crown prince's camel, horse, hawk, and dog yards. In less than a year he had risen to grand general, third rank.

sentences.zh: 及先天二年七月，毛仲預誅蕭、岑等功，授輔國大將軍、左武衛大將軍、檢校內外閑廄兼知監牧使，進封霍國公，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: By the seventh month of the second year of Xiantian, for Maozhong's merit in executing Xiao, Cen, and others, he was appointed Assistant State General, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard, commissioner inspecting inner and outer stud farms and also supervising pastures, advanced Duke of Huo, substantive fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Xiantian, for his part in putting down Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and the rest, Maozhong was made assistant state general and grand general of the left martial guard, with charge of all stud farms and pasture administration, and was advanced to Duke of Huo with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 毛仲奉公正直，不避權貴，兩營萬騎功臣、閑廄官吏皆懼其威，人不敢犯。

translations.literal: Maozhong embraced fairness and uprightness and did not avoid the powerful; meritorious subjects of the two Ten Thousand Rider camps and stud farm officials all feared his awesomeness, and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong was upright and fearless before the mighty. The meritorious men of both Ten Thousand Rider camps and the stud officials all feared him, and none dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 苑中營田草萊常收，率皆豐溢，玄宗以為能。

translations.literal: Park camp farmland and weeds were constantly harvested; yields were mostly abundant overflow; Xuanzong considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: The park farms and fallow ground under his charge yielded abundantly, and Xuanzong judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年，贈其父秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year of Kaiyuan, posthumously granted his father as Governor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan his father was posthumously made governor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 毛仲雖有賜莊宅，奴婢、駝馬、錢帛不可勝紀，常於閑廄側內宅住。

translations.literal: Though Maozhong had bestowed estates and mansions, slaves, camels, horses, cash and silks beyond counting, he constantly lived in the inner residence beside the stud farms.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had been granted estates and mansions and possessed slaves, camels, horses, and treasure beyond reckoning, he usually lived in a private house beside the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 每入侍宴賞，與諸王、姜皎等禦幄前連榻而坐。

translations.literal: Each time entering to attend feasts and rewards, with the princes and Jiang Jiao and others before the imperial curtains he joined couches to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended banquets he sat on shared couches with the princes and Jiang Jiao before the imperial curtains.

sentences.zh: 玄宗或時不見，則悄然如有所失；

translations.literal: If Xuanzong sometimes did not see him, then silently as if something were lost;
translations.idiomatic: If Xuanzong did not see him for a time, he fell quiet as though something were missing;

sentences.zh: 見之則歡洽連宵，有至日晏。

translations.literal: when he saw him, joy was intimate through the night, sometimes until the sun declined.
translations.idiomatic: when he did, their joy ran through the night, sometimes until sundown.

sentences.zh: 其妻已邑虢國夫人；

translations.literal: His wife was already enfeoffed Lady of Guo State;
translations.idiomatic: His wife had already been made Lady of Guo;

sentences.zh: 賜妻李氏又為國夫人。

translations.literal: His granted wife Lady Li was also made a state lady.
translations.idiomatic: and his consort Lady Li was likewise granted the title of state lady.

sentences.zh: 每入內朝謁，二夫人同承賜賫，生男，孩稚已授五品，與皇太子同遊，故中官楊思勖、高力士等常避畏之。

translations.literal: Each time entering the inner court for audience, both ladies together received imperial gifts; when sons were born, infants already granted fifth rank, playing with the Crown Prince; thus eunuchs Yang Sixun, Gao Lishi, and others constantly avoided and feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended court audience both wives received imperial gifts together. His infant sons were given fifth rank while still in the cradle and played with the crown prince, so eunuchs such as Yang Sixun and Gao Lishi kept their distance in fear.

sentences.zh: 七年，進位特進，行太仆卿，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Seventh year, advanced to Exceptional Advancement, acting Minister of the Imperial Stud; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was advanced to exceptional grand master and acting minister of the imperial stud; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 九年，持節充朔方道防禦討擊大使，仍以左領軍大總管王晙與天兵軍節度張說，東與幽州節度裴伷先等計會。

translations.literal: Ninth year, bearing the staff as ShuoFang circuit defense and strike commissioner; still with Left Wing Army Grand Commander Wang Jun and Tianbing army commander Zhang Yue, eastward coordinating with Youzhou commander Pei Youxian and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he bore imperial credentials as defense and strike commissioner on the ShuoFang circuit, while Wang Jun, grand commander of the left wing army, and Zhang Yue, commander of the Tianbing army, coordinated eastward with Pei Youxian of Youzhou and the rest.

sentences.zh: 毛仲部統嚴整，群牧孳息，遂數倍其初。

translations.literal: Maozhong's command was strict and orderly; the herds multiplied, thus several times the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong's administration was strict and orderly, and the herds multiplied until they were several times their former number.

sentences.zh: 芻粟之類，不敢盜竊，每歲回殘，常致數萬斛。

translations.literal: Fodder and grain—none dared steal; each year's surplus often reached tens of thousands of hu.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared steal fodder or grain, and each year's surplus often ran to tens of thousands of hu.

sentences.zh: 不三年，扈從東封，以諸牧馬數萬匹從，每色為一隊，望如雲錦，玄宗益喜。

translations.literal: Within not three years he followed the eastern feng sacrifice, with several tens of thousands of stud horses following; each color one company; viewed like clouds of brocade; Xuanzong was increasingly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In less than three years he accompanied the eastern feng rites with tens of thousands of stud horses, each color formed into its own column, a sight like brocaded clouds, and Xuanzong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 於嶽下以宰相源乾曜、張說加左右丞相，毛仲加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the foot of the mountain the chief ministers Yuan Qianyao and Zhang Yue were added as left and right chancellors; Maozhong was added Same Glory with the Government as opening office.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the sacred mountain the chief ministers Yuan Qianyao and Zhang Yue were made left and right chancellors, and Maozhong was given the rank of same glory with the government as opening office.

sentences.zh: 自玄宗先天正位後，以後父王同皎及姚崇、宋璟及毛仲十五年間四人至開府，又敕張說為《監牧頌》以美之。

translations.literal: From Xuanzong's orthodox assumption after Xiantian, among the empress's father Wang Tongjiao and Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong, within fifteen years four men reached opening office; also ordered Zhang Yue to compose the 'Ode on Pasture Supervision' to praise it.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuanzong's accession after Xiantian until this time, only four men in fifteen years had reached opening office: the empress's father Wang Tongjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong. The emperor also ordered Zhang Yue to compose an ode on pasture supervision in his praise.

sentences.zh: 十七年，從朝五陵，又贈毛仲父益州大都督。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, followed the court to the five mausoleums; again posthumously granted Maozhong's father as Governor-General of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he followed the court to the five imperial tombs, and Maozhong's father was again posthumously made governor-general of Yi.

sentences.zh: 毛仲益驕，嘗求為兵部尚書，玄宗不悅，毛仲怏怏，見於詞色。

translations.literal: Maozhong grew more arrogant; once sought to be Minister of War; Xuanzong was displeased; Maozhong was resentful, shown in words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong grew ever more arrogant and once asked to be minister of war. Xuanzong was displeased, and Maozhong's resentment showed in his words and bearing.

sentences.zh: 又福順子娶毛仲女，宜德、唐地文等數十人皆與毛仲善，倚之多為不法。

translations.literal: Also Fushun's son married Maozhong's daughter; Yide, Tang Diwen, and several tens of others were all friendly with Maozhong; relying on him many did unlawful things.
translations.idiomatic: Fushun's son married Maozhong's daughter, and Yide, Tang Diwen, and dozens of others were on close terms with him. Relying on his power, many of them broke the law.

sentences.zh: 中官等妒其全盛逾己，專發其罪，尤倨慢之。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were jealous that their complete flourishing exceeded themselves, exclusively exposed their crimes, and especially treated them with arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs envied his surpassing glory and set about exposing his crimes, treating him with especial arrogance.

sentences.zh: 中官高品者，毛仲視之蔑如也；

translations.literal: Eunuchs of high rank—Maozhong viewed them with contempt;
translations.idiomatic: High-ranking eunuchs he treated with contempt;

sentences.zh: 如卑品者，小忤意則挫辱如己之僮仆。

translations.literal: those of low rank, at a small offense of will he humiliated them like his own bond servants.
translations.idiomatic: low-ranking ones he humiliated at the slightest provocation like his own household slaves.

sentences.zh: 力士輩恨入骨髓。

translations.literal: Lishi and his cohort hated him to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi and his fellows hated him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 毛仲承恩遇，妻產，嘗借苑中亭子納涼，玄宗借之。

translations.literal: Maozhong received grace and favor; when his wife bore a child he once borrowed a pavilion in the park for cool shade; Xuanzong lent it.
translations.idiomatic: Honored by the emperor, Maozhong once borrowed a pavilion in the imperial park when his wife was in labor so she could keep cool, and Xuanzong granted it.

sentences.zh: 中官構之彌甚，曰：「北門奴官太盛，豪者皆一心，不除之，必起大患。」

translations.literal: Eunuchs framed him ever more, saying: 'Northern gate slave officials are too flourishing; the bold are all of one mind—if not removed, great calamity will surely rise.'
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs slandered him all the more, saying, "The slave officials of the northern gate have grown too powerful. Their boldest men are of one mind. Unless they are removed, great disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 後毛仲索甲仗於太原軍器監，時嚴挺之為少尹，奏之。

translations.literal: Later Maozhong sought armor and weapons from the Taiyuan armory supervisor; at that time Yan Tingzhi was Vice Governor and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Maozhong requisitioned arms from the Taiyuan armory. Yan Tingzhi, then vice governor, reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗恐其黨震懼為亂，乃隱其實狀，詔曰：「開府儀同三司、兼殿中監、霍國公、內外閑廄監牧都使王毛仲，是惟微細，非有功績，擢自家臣，升於朝位。

translations.literal: Xuanzong feared their faction, alarmed, might rebel; he concealed the true situation and edicted: 'Same Glory with the Government as opening office, also Director of the Palace Directorate, Duke of Huo, superintendent of inner and outer stud farms and pastures Wang Maozhong is only minute and slight, without meritorious deeds; promoted from a household servant to court position.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that his faction might panic and rise in revolt, Xuanzong concealed the true facts and issued an edict: "Wang Maozhong, opening office of same glory with the government, director of the palace directorate, Duke of Huo, and superintendent of all stud farms and pastures, is a man of no account and no merit. Raised from a household slave to court rank,

sentences.zh: 恩寵莫二，委任斯崇。

translations.literal: Grace and favor unmatched, commission and trust supremely lofty.
translations.idiomatic: he has enjoyed favor beyond compare and trust beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 無涓塵之益，肆驕盈之誌。

translations.literal: Without the benefit of a speck of dust, he unrestrainedly indulged proud overflow ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He has rendered not the slightest service, yet indulged boundless pride.

sentences.zh: 往屬艱難，遽茲逃匿，念深惟舊，義在優容，仍荷殊榮，蔑聞悛悔。

translations.literal: Formerly when difficulties belonged to him he abruptly thus fled and hid; thinking deeply of old ties, righteousness lay in indulgent tolerance; still bearing special glory, he heeded no word of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: In former days of peril he fled and hid, yet remembering old ties I showed him indulgence and still heaped honor on him. He has shown no sign of repentance.

sentences.zh: 在公無竭盡之效，居常多怨望之詞。

translations.literal: In public office no effect of exhausting service; in daily life many resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: In office he has never given his all; in private he utters constant complaint.

sentences.zh: 跡其深愆，合從誅殛；

translations.literal: Tracing his deep crimes, he should follow execution;
translations.idiomatic: Weighed against his grave offenses, he deserves death;

sentences.zh: 恕其庸昧，宜從遠貶。

translations.literal: Pardoning his mediocrity and dullness, he should follow distant banishment.
translations.idiomatic: yet pardoning his dull wits, he is banished to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 可瀼州別駕員外置長任，差使馳驛領送至任，忽許東西及判事。」

translations.literal: May be Vice Prefect of Rang on extra roster for long tenure; dispatch a courier by post horse to escort him to his post; hastily permit east-west travel and adjudication matters.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed acting vice prefect of Rang for an indefinite term. A courier shall escort him to his post by relay horse. He is permitted to travel and to hear cases.

sentences.zh: 左領軍大將軍耿國公葛福順，貶壁州員外別駕；

translations.literal: Left Wing Army Grand General Duke of Geng Ge Fushun, demoted external Vice Prefect of Bi;
translations.idiomatic: Ge Fushun, grand general of the left wing army and Duke of Geng, was demoted to acting vice prefect of Bi;
