sentences.zh: 左監門將軍盧龍子唐地文，貶振州員外別駕；

translations.literal: Left Gate Guard General Son of Lu Long Tang Diwen, demoted external Vice Prefect of Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Diwen, general of the left gate guard and son of Lu Long, to acting vice prefect of Zhen;

sentences.zh: 右武衛將軍成紀侯李守德，貶嚴州員外別駕，守德，本宜德也，立功後改名；

translations.literal: Right Martial Guard General Marquis of Chengji Li Shoude, demoted external Vice Prefect of Yan—Shoude was originally Yide and renamed after merit;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shoude, general of the right martial guard and Marquis of Chengji, to acting vice prefect of Yan—Shoude had originally been called Yide and took a new name after his merit;

sentences.zh: 右威衛將軍王景耀，貶黨州員外別駕；

translations.literal: Right Majestic Guard General Wang Jingyao, demoted external Vice Prefect of Dang;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingyao, general of the right majestic guard, to acting vice prefect of Dang;

sentences.zh: 右威衛將軍高廣濟，貶道州員外別駕。

translations.literal: Right Majestic Guard General Gao Guangji, demoted external Vice Prefect of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: and Gao Guangji, general of the right majestic guard, to acting vice prefect of Dao.

sentences.zh: 毛仲男太子仆守貞，貶施州司戶；

translations.literal: Maozhong's son Crown Prince Stud Keeper Shouzhen, demoted Registrar of Shi;
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong's son Shouzhen, keeper of the crown prince's stud, was demoted to registrar of Shi;

sentences.zh: 太子家令守廉，貶溪州司戶；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Household Chief Shouli, demoted Registrar of Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Shouli, chief of the crown prince's household, to registrar of Xi;

sentences.zh: 率更令守慶，貶鶴州司倉；

translations.literal: Court of the Imperial Clan Vice Director Shouqing, demoted Granary Officer of He;
translations.idiomatic: Shouqing, vice director of the court of the imperial clan, to granary officer of He;

sentences.zh: 左監門長史守道，貶涪州參軍。

translations.literal: Left Gate Guard Senior Recorder Shoudao, demoted military adjutant of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: and Shoudao, senior recorder of the left gate guard, to military adjutant of Fu.

sentences.zh: 連累者數十人。

translations.literal: Those implicated numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen others were implicated.

sentences.zh: 又詔殺毛仲，及永州而縊之。

translations.literal: Also edicted to kill Maozhong; at Yong he was strangled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered Maozhong's death. At Yong he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李林甫以諂佞進身，位極臺輔，不懼盈滿，蔽主聰明，生既唯務陷人，死亦為人所陷，得非彼蒼假手，以示禍淫者乎！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Linfu by flattery advanced, position utmost as platform aide, not fearing fullness, blinding the lord's clarity; in life only scheming to trap others, in death also trapped by others—is it not that Heaven lent hands to show punishment of excess?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Li Linfu rose by flattery to the highest office. Unafraid of excess, he blinded his sovereign. In life he schemed only to destroy others; in death he was destroyed in turn. Was this not Heaven borrowing human hands to punish the wicked?

sentences.zh: 楊國忠稟性奸回，才薄行穢，領四十余使，恣弄威權，天子莫見其非，群臣由之杜口，致祿山叛逆，鑾輅播遷，梟首覆宗，莫救艱步。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong by nature was treacherous and crooked, talent thin and conduct foul; headed forty-plus offices, wantonly wielded awesomeness and power; the Son of Heaven did not see his faults, court ministers thereby sealed their mouths, causing An Lushan's rebellion, the imperial carriage scattered in exile, head displayed and clan overturned, none could save the hard step.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was treacherous by nature, mean in talent and foul in conduct. He held more than forty offices and wielded power at will. The emperor saw no fault in him, and the ministers fell silent. He brought on An Lushan's rebellion, the flight of the throne, the display of his head and the ruin of his clan, and none could save the dynasty in its extremity.

sentences.zh: 以玄宗之睿哲，而惑於二人者，蓋巧言令色，先意承旨，財利誘之，迷而不悟也。

translations.literal: That with Xuanzong's sagely clarity he was yet deluded by two men—cover because clever words and pleasing color, anticipating intent and receiving instructions, wealth and profit tempting them, lost and not awakened.
translations.idiomatic: That even one as sagacious as Xuanzong was misled by these two men was because they spoke smoothly, looked pleasing, anticipated his wishes, and tempted him with wealth until he was lost and could not wake.

sentences.zh: 開元任姚崇、宋璟而治，幸林甫、國忠而亂，與夫齊桓任管仲、隰朋，幸豎刁、易牙，亦何異哉！

translations.literal: Kaiyuan employed Yao Chong and Song Jing and was governed; fortunate in Linfu and Guozhong and was chaotic—with Duke Huan of Qi employing Guan Zhong and Xi Peng, fortunate in Shu Diao and Yi Ya—what difference?
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan he employed Yao Chong and Song Jing and the realm was governed; he favored Linfu and Guozhong and fell into chaos. How was this different from Duke Huan of Qi, who employed Guan Zhong and Xi Peng but favored Shu Diao and Yi Ya?

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「臣有作福作威，害於而家，兇於而國。」

translations.literal: The Book says: 'When ministers make blessings and make awesomeness, they harm your family and are bane to your state.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "When ministers make blessings and wield power for themselves, they harm your house and bring ruin to your state.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「佞人殆。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Flatterers are dangerous.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Flatterers are dangerous."

sentences.zh: 誠哉是言也。

translations.literal: Truly is this saying.
translations.idiomatic: How true those words are.

sentences.zh: 張暐、王琚、王毛仲，皆鄧通、閎孺之流也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, Wang Ju, and Wang Maozhong were all of the stream of Deng Tong and Hong Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, Wang Ju, and Wang Maozhong were all men of the sort of Deng Tong and Hong Ru.

sentences.zh: 琚有締構之功，過多僭侈，死於非罪，亦何惜之！

translations.literal: Ju had merit of binding together the framework; excess of usurpation and luxury; died in unmerited crime—what is there to pity!
translations.idiomatic: Ju had helped bind the realm together, but his excess and presumption were great, and he died for crimes he had not committed. What is there to pity?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天啟亂階，甫、忠當國。

translations.literal: The praise says: Heaven opened the ladder of disorder; Linfu and Guozhong held the state.
translations.idiomatic: Praise says: Heaven opened the way to chaos; Linfu and Guozhong held power.

sentences.zh: 蔽主聰明，秉心讒慝。

translations.literal: Blinding the lord's clarity, holding hearts of slanderous evil.
translations.idiomatic: They blinded their sovereign's judgment and harbored slander in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 暐同二王，亦承恩德。

translations.literal: Wei, like the two Wangs, also received grace and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, like the two Wangs, also received imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 籲哉僭逾，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Alas, excess of presumption, not knowing the limit of law.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for their presumption beyond all bounds, heedless of measure and law.
